The power of data in trading protocol selection
With the launch of various generative AI chatbots, the expectations around AI and its applications have changed. But what about the bond trading world? Can a conventional AI chatbot tell you when to PT or not to PT? No—But the MarketAxess platform can help you decide.
By leveraging our data driven solutions—both on pricing and liquidity metrics—you gain valuable, real-time insights into current market dynamics, giving actionable, tradeable insights into when to PT and when to use another protocol.
The solutions we offer help you choose what the best protocol is to meet your execution objectives. It also guides you to choose the best approach on how to manage your risk—what to trade, when to trade, and how to trade effectively—even if PT is not the best avenue. Our platform does the heavy lifting for you by combining the best-in-class raw data, leveraging our platform and TraX® data with AI-driven metrics like CP+™ and Tradability, to arm you with the tools to achieve the best execution outcome for every trade.
CP+ and CP+ Inquiry are pre-trade TCA indicators informing you of expected costs of trading:

- CP+ is our proprietary AI-powered pricing engine for corporate bonds. It produces an unbiased, two-sided market for more than 33,000 instruments worldwide. With CP+ you know where the market is for a given bond, helping achieve your portfolio construction objectives. CP+ bid-offer spread is a good indicator of the liquidity and market activity on each bond.

- CP+ Inquiry is an expansion of CP+ that is size specific and brings extra granularity to the pre-trade costs of trading, tailored to your sizes. With accurate and real-time data available at both the portfolio and bond level, you can predict and tailor your portfolio trades to your unique specifications.

- With Relative Liquidity Score, you can stay up-to-date on the liquidity of the bonds in your portfolio and identify illiquid securities. It is calibrated on traded volume in the market and is an indication of market turnover over a period.

- Tradability adds an order-specific dimension to Relative Liquidity Score when quantifying the liquidity– showing you the depth of liquidity available given the size and direction of your orders. Tradability also informs you of the skew in the market (by looking at the delta between tradability on your side vs the opposite side). It helps you better understand the market’s capacity to fulfil your order. It shows you when the market is right for your PT or whether you’re better off trading this basket as a List.

- Finally, compare your order size with the traded volume in TraX to obtain a pre-trade estimate of your market’s impact.

With our comprehensive data suite, you have pre-trade estimates of your costs, an overview of the distribution of liquidity allowing you to adjust your list where required by removing or adding bonds. Our data solutions can also be used pre-trade, during the trade, and post-trade to drill into your execution outcomes. Understanding your TCA is key to refining what to trade as well as how and when to trade it.
While the PT is still live, our Outlier Analysis tab on the platform allows clients to visualize the pricing performance line by line. It automatically filters on bonds which are priced further away from CP+. Clients can make decisions efficiently as we created this quick feedback loop on dealer pricing which is highly pertinent for large PT lists. You can also filter the less liquid bond based on our metrics to view the pricing outcomes on those specific items.
For post-trade analysis, we produce a TCA report after the trade is done so that you can conduct deep analysis and look at your PT performance under various criteria. The TCA also allows clients to compare PT execution from 1 trade to another.
With AI-powered analytics at your fingertips—coupled with best-in-class market data and liquidity—there is no better place to trade. Think of it as a one-stop shop for optimal protocol selection.

title: Validating systematic fixed income strategies with the right data
text:
Validating systematic fixed income strategies with the right data
Data is a key prerequisite to creating and running systematic strategies. Without data, the strategy cannot build or subsequently respect a rules-based structure. Reflecting on traditional systematic trading products, each one typically has robust and available data which, in several cases, is drawn from trading exchanges and then applied to the strategy. This availability of data, alongside the respective market’s trading structure, has meant that systematic strategies have remained relatively nascent in fixed income credit. However, recently this has changed as fixed income electronic platforms have enriched existing data sets and built sophisticated data tools – tools which mean systematic strategies can prosper in fixed income.

The fixed income credit market does not yet possess trading exchanges like those in the equity markets. Instead it relies heavily on voice execution and, increasingly, electronic trading systems, like MarketAxess. Estimates from Greenwich Associates, the independent research group, show that electronic trading in US credit is now approximately 30% of market volume, up from 20% a year ago. This shift in execution structure means that bond trading venues possess an increasingly valuable data set from which they can build more sophisticated and insightful tools. In addition, the same trading venues have built tools that enrichen data available as a result of regulatory rules, such as TRACE in the US. It is the combination of these tools which creates data sets which have not previously been available in fixed income credit. In turn this has created an opportunity for firms to use the data to build and run systematic investment strategies.

Leveraging a consultative approach together with the expertise of our data scientists, MarketAxess has worked with several clients looking to confirm the potential opportunity for a systematic fixed income credit strategy. For example, MarketAxess can combine the historical data available within MarketAxess’ AI-powered pricing engine Composite+™ alongside enriched TRACE data to create a more compelling picture of prior market activity alongside predictive pricing indicators. This type of data availability and analysis is giving funds unique inputs allowing them to assess the opportunity across sectors, industries and even individual bonds. With hundreds of thousands of individual bonds available in the credit market, it’s hard to know which will maximise your strategy, hence why collaborating with clients is so crucial to find success. Assuming such data validates the opportunity, the same data can in turn be consumed and employed for the live strategy via API, FTP or through MarketAxess’ Excel add-in.

Data allows systematic funds to see through the fog, establishing the validity and viability of the strategy. The same data then allows assessment of live market opportunities, framed within the rules of the strategy. It is the enrichment of existing data by vendors alongside the construction and development of their own bespoke solutions which has helped fill data gaps left as a result of different regulatory regimes or comparably opaque market trading dynamics and data capture. These continued improvements in data leave fixed income systematic credit strategies with cleaner, clearer signals upon which to execute.

title: What if fixed income ETF baskets could mimic the index with accurate real-time NAVs, premiums and discounts?
text:
What if fixed income ETF baskets could mimic the index with accurate real-time NAVs, premiums and discounts?
One of the most significant differences between fixed income and equity ETFs is the creation/redemption experience. Typically, with equity ETFs, a market maker knows exactly what constitutes a valid basket – both security and size. The basket composition doesn’t tend to change for size, daily activity or side. Essentially, the basket is the index. With fixed income ETFs, the baskets that are exchanged for creation and redemption units are, more often than not, customized baskets that are a subset of the overall index. If basketing activity is especially heavy on a given day, a market maker may have to wait to receive a transactable basket that would hedge their risk. This mismatch between the immediate transparency of the exchange-traded ETF shares and the OTC nature of the underlying securities creates market inefficiencies.

Enter MarketAxess CP+™ and eNAV

Our breadth of liquidity data and the real-time pricing capability of CP+ (fka Composite+), put us in a unique position to build indices that are comprised of tradeable securities which are priced accurately in real-time. This enables fixed income ETF issuers to offer ETFs where the baskets are the actual index, much like equity ETFs currently. With baskets comprised of tradeable constituents that are supported by real-time CP+ pricing, we can also offer real-time NAVs for the funds, or eNAVs, via our partnership with Virtu. Combining real-time eNAVs with live ETF share pricing allows us to offer real-time premiums and discounts for a suite of tradeable ETFs. And because the eNAV is calculated using a transactable basket, market makers can make more competitive markets. These improvements in pricing and accessibility of bonds will help advance the fixed income and ETF industries so that they are on par with the equity markets.

title: What if fixed income index constituents traded on live order books with visible depth of market?
text:
What if fixed income index constituents traded on live order books with visible depth of market?
I’m frequently reminded about the lessons fixed income credit market can learn from equities. Our President and COO, Chris Concannon, has an equity market background and is very open about the topic. One difference between the two markets that he is known to highlight is the contrast between the prevalent trading protocols. In equities, participants generally post levels at which they wish to trade (aggressors provide liquidity). In fixed income, the participants generally request levels where the market will trade (aggressors take liquidity). It’s a subtle but significant difference and it reinforces the dichotomy in liquidity profiles of the two markets. There are a number of reasons why the credit market hasn’t offered a protocol whereby institutional investors can efficiently express their intentions in this way (not enough data, too many cusips, etc). MarketAxess believes the credit market is poised to overcome these hurdles, adopt an equity-like trading protocol and bring about greater price transparency.

Enter MarketAxess and Live Markets

Live Markets is the first order book, click-to-trade protocol for institutional credit markets. Dealers, ETF market makers and the buy side can now anonymously stream or enter one or two-sided markets into an order book that is fully visible to our extensive client base. This creates unique trading opportunities but also significant amounts of pricing content.

What does this mean for fixed income indexing?

As we laid out in the earlier blogs, fixed income indexing has always struggled with timely and accurate pricing of the underlying constituents. Levels posted in Live Markets are fully executable with the ability to “sweep the stack”. This means that if all of an investable index’s constituents are populated on Live Markets, an index trader (ETF, TRS or basket) that is coded to our APIs will have the ability to instantaneously value index trades of various sizes. Imagine a client asks a dealer to quote $100 and $200 million of an index. The dealer will have visibility down the stack to size and price the hedge of both sizes. Imagine an ETF market maker being able to automate the execution of a basket much the way they do in equity ETFs today. Imagine an ETF Issuer being able to display the liquidity of the basket underlying a new small ETF as opposed to the liquidity of the ETF shares themselves (which traditionally would be narrow for a new, small ETF). Live Markets will help to evolve the fixed income indexing space by addressing these issues in the market.

title: What if fixed income index constituents were accurately priced in real-time?
text:
What if fixed income index constituents were accurately priced in real-time?
Fixed income indices generally provide an official valuation once per day. Historically this has been because pricing for the underlying constituents wasn’t available outside of published end-of-day prices. Given the OTC nature and infrequent trading of some bonds, even one-time end-of-day pricing can be challenging. With advances in pricing capabilities and demand from the market, predominantly ETF Market Makers who need to provide real-time liquidity for the ETF shares, some pricing vendors began providing pricing at more frequent intervals during the trading day. However, the challenges around data availability, modeling capabilities and subsequently, accuracy, remain.

Enter MarketAxess and CP+™

Our unique position within the capital markets and electronic credit trading market share of over 70%, give us a broader view of pricing inputs than competitors. Approximately 20% of TRACE-reported US IG volumes and 12% of US HY volumes are executed on our platform. Not only do we have access to the TRACE-reported data for these trades, we see all prices submitted for a given inquiry which provides greater visibility into depth of market leading to more accurate real-time pricing. Additionally, our unique vantage point helps better understand the context and pricing implications for non-standard trade patterns such as dealer-initiated transactions. We have been able to harness all this data with a machine learning algorithm that produces two-sided markets every 15-60 seconds for the vast majority of TRACE volumes. The access to additional data points combined with the innovative approach to modeling bond pricing has allowed MarketAxess to quickly build CP+ into a recognized leader in real time valuation of fixed income securities.

What does this mean for fixed income indexing?

We have already seen the impact of accurate real-time pricing as clients have embraced CP+ as a pricing benchmark in our auto-execution and crossing trading protocols. As we roll out indices that utilize CP+ as the pricing source, the intra-day transparency will provide significantly greater confidence to market participants as to where they can execute while also providing where those constituents will be officially marked at end-of-day. With increased certainty around pricing comes lower execution costs and tighter markets. When accurate real-time prices are combined with investable index construction, fixed income indexing and index products can trade more like equity indices. This means transparent execution and hedging costs, the potential for full index baskets which eliminate basis risk and timely basket negotiations, the potential for real-time indices and greater velocity of trading for credit vehicles. Most market participants recognize the impediments holding back fixed income index trading. We feel that CP+ removes the most significant hurdle and will help usher in a new stage for bond indexing.

title: What if fixed income indices were comprised of securities that were tradable?
text:
What if fixed income indices were comprised of securities that were tradable?
One of the more widely followed US investment grade corporate bond indices is comprised of more than 6,500 securities and a popular broad US. high yield corporate bond index includes almost 2,000 securities. Even “liquid” investment grade and high yield indices can include around 2,000 and 1,000 bonds, respectively. The issue is that these indices were generally created for use by active managers that weren’t necessarily focused on the liquidity of the constituents and therefore the tradability of the bonds themselves. After all, active management entails the selection of a subset of a universe, not investment across the entire universe.

With the consistent growth of the fixed income ETF market and the expansion of electronic trading, “beta” trading has become more prevalent in the fixed income market. However, the issue with trading existing credit indices and products is that the illiquid tails of the indices present difficulties in pricing, sourcing and hedging, which leads to greater costs and less efficient markets. These investment challenges are also prevalent for newer investment strategies, like smart beta or those based around ESG and green bonds. Smart or alternative beta models can identify a subset of securities as attractive or inefficiently priced when lack of liquidity is the predominant issue. This further highlights the need for accurate data to ensure that the securities identified by these newer strategies are actually available to trade when needed most.

So how can MarketAxess help? While we can’t make bonds magically appear on bid lists, we can help better define benchmarks and expectations.

Because of our unique position within credit markets, MarketAxess has greater insight into the tradability of individual securities and the construction of accessible betas or indices. For example, greater than 20% of the daily TRACE-reported trading volume in US investment grade corporate bonds occurs on MarketAxess. Unlike other market participants that have access to TRACE-supplied details for these trades (price, size, dealer or client direction) MarketAxess has additional data points including whether the trade was offer-wanted or bid wanted, number of responses and prices for each response. Potentially more powerful is the access to similar data for inquiries that DNT’d (did not trade) on our platform as TRACE provides no visibility. We have incorporated this data into unique products (Composite+™, Relative Liquidity Scores) which are the backbone of our index construction process and lead to our advantage in constructing tradeable indices.

Credit markets are evolving with smarter trading protocols and more defined investment strategies. Index construction needs to evolve as well.

title: Why AI won’t take your fixed income job
text:
Why AI won’t take your fixed income job
A conversation with ChatGPT.

There's been so much talk about how AI could replace human workers across virtually every industry sector, from telecoms to retail to trucking and beyond. Lately, following the proliferation of generative AI, the conversation has turned to us, and whether AI might affect fixed income jobs. So, I figured I should have a conversation with ChatGPT, the ubiquitous AI chatbot, to see what’s in store for my fixed income career. ChatGPT is a bit long winded, so I’ll just provide the interesting bits.

Me: Will AI take my fixed income job?

ChatGPT: AI is best suited for tasks that involve repetitive, rule-based processes, such as data analysis, pattern recognition, and decision-making. These are tasks that can be automated to increase efficiency and accuracy, potentially reducing the need for human intervention.

However, there are other aspects of fixed income jobs that require human skills and judgment, such as relationship building with clients, communication, and problem-solving.

It sounds like AI can’t do soft skills and problem solving, which is good for me since that’s the fun part of my job. Perhaps AI is more of a helper than a replacement—something that can handle the time consuming or mundane parts of our jobs, freeing up time for us to innovate and collaborate with clients.

Me: Which fixed income tasks can AI help automate?

ChatGPT:

1. Portfolio Management: AI can assist with portfolio management tasks, such as identifying investment opportunities, conducting risk assessments, and optimizing portfolio allocations based on market conditions.

2. Risk Management: AI can analyze data related to fixed income securities and identify potential risks that could impact investment returns.

3. Trading: AI can automate fixed income trading by using algorithms to analyze market data and identify trading opportunities.

4. Credit Analysis: AI can assist with credit analysis by analyzing financial statements, credit ratings, and other relevant data to assess the creditworthiness of issuers of fixed income securities.

5. Compliance Monitoring: AI can assist with compliance monitoring by analyzing transactions and other data to identify potential regulatory issues or violations.

I’m not sure if ChatGPT is bragging or what, but that’s an impressive list. At MarketAxess, I work on CP™+, our AI-driven real-time fixed income pricing, which is used in the first three areas. Large dealers and algo funds use CP+ data in their own AI models to optimize trading strategies. Similarly, clients are creating AI models with our CP+ data to identify patterns in the market to inform their investment decisions and track portfolio risk in real-time. With more than 50 million levels per day, price updates as fast as every 15 seconds and 100% coverage in its markets, CP+ is taking these workflows to new levels of efficiency and scale.

My fixed income career may still have some legs! But there are a lot of choices for fixed income data out there, so what’s the difference? One would think that better quality data would lead to better AI results…

Me: Does AI need good data to work?

ChatGPT: Yes, AI needs good data to work effectively. In fact, the quality of the data used to train an AI model is one of the most important factors in determining the accuracy and performance of the model. If the data used to train an AI model is biased, incomplete, or otherwise flawed, the model's predictions and decisions may be inaccurate or unreliable. On the other hand, if the data is of high quality, the AI model will be better equipped to learn the patterns and relationships needed to make accurate predictions and decisions.

Our data products leverage unique and quantifiable trading insights from our platform (think depth of book). This data eclipses what you see in trades alone. In Europe, we also use our TraX market data as a key input for CP+. Unique data + strong models (yes, we use AI models too) = high quality data products. The numbers support it too: last year more than 20% of trades on the MarketAxess platform used CP+ Auto-X™ trading protocols.

While it dawned on me that ChatGPT (a.k.a. the AI talking robot) has some major conflicts of interest in this discussion, I think the conclusion is irrefutable—AI is driving greater efficiency in the fixed income market. But it’s not going to take your job, or mine, just yet.

title: Why systematic strategies are the next big thing in fixed income
text:
Why systematic strategies are the next big thing in fixed income
Fixed income credit investment and trading has changed substantially over the past decade and a half with recent changes leading to the increased viability of systematic strategies. The global financial crisis and subsequent events have irreversibly changed fixed income market structure giving rise to increased automation, as well as a growth in alternative liquidity providers and electronic trading venues.

The way in which investors seek to allocate capital has also evolved, as have the strategies they favour and the returns they expect. This has been most evident in the ‘rise of passive’ credit investment, as well as the growing penetration and assets-under-management of ETF asset managers. However, a strategy previously reserved for other asset classes has recently started to make greater inroads in fixed income credit – Systematic. 

Systematic investing has become more applicable to fixed income credit precisely as a result of the market structure changes taking place. Through the growth of alternative liquidity providers – and, vitally, because electronic platforms can now connect end-investors to that alternative and/or natural liquidity – fixed income systematic credit strategies now have a higher likelihood of execution when signals are received. In essence, systematic trading strategies can realistically be employed and the signals won’t be wasted.

MarketAxess Open Trading™, the anonymous all-to-all trading marketplace, plays a key role here as the market leader in connecting end-investors to natural and alternative liquidity sources, which they would not otherwise be able to access. Open Trading is uniquely placed to assist systematic strategies with asset sourcing (or offloading) and the subsequent alpha capture/defence within this new market structure. 

Alongside this developing execution landscape, markedly better-quality data is helping to improve signal generation and accuracy. The improved quality and cleanliness of the data assists in validating the applicability and profitability of prospective systematic strategies and, once launched, the same data allows those strategies to identify live and relevant signals and act accordingly. Choosing the ‘right’ data is important – not all data is of equal applicability, especially in markets where regulatory reporting requirements differ. In this regard, MarketAxess Data Solutions via Trax and its multi-market predictive composite pricing tool, Composite+, (which provides over 30 million levels per day), provides data through which signals can be deciphered. 

Contrary to some suspicions, systematic fixed income investment does not always seek to eradicate the role of ‘humans’ from the investment process – rather it seeks to apply human input where its value is most keenly felt. Although substantial changes have occurred, fixed income credit remains relatively illiquid when set against standard commodity trading advisor (CTA) trading products, underlining the requirement for some level of human involvement.

Equally, the strategies are not black-box, mysterious operations. Without devaluing the complexity involved, particularly with regards the construction of the machines, the machine processes must be simple to the extent that they can be explained. However, what is undoubtedly true is that as the global investment landscape keeps evolving and potentially becomes yet more complex, the foundations are laid for fixed income systematic credit strategies to prosper.

title: Arcesium Integrates Additional MarketAxess Data and Analytics to Enhance Fixed Income Workflows
text:
Arcesium Integrates Additional MarketAxess Data and Analytics to
 Enhance Fixed Income Workflows

 Newest integration designed to streamline fixed income workflows for hedge funds, institutional asset
 managers and capital markets firms

NEW YORK, October 7, 2026 — Arcesium, a leading global financial technology provider to the
investment industry, today announced an integration with MarketAxess Holdings Inc. (Nasdaq: MKTX), a
leading electronic trading platform for fixed income securities, to provide investment firms with seamless
data solutions across the fixed income trade lifecycle. With the integration of MarketAxess CP+™ and
TraX® market data into Arcesium’s Aquata ® and Opterra® platforms, hedge funds, institutional asset
managers and capital markets firms can now connect front-to-back workflows and improve data accuracy
across investment and operational processes.

The integration with Arcesium’s platforms enables mutual clients to embed MarketAxess’ pricing, liquidity
and transaction data directly into their fixed income operational workflows. MarketAxess CP+ is an AI-
powered algorithmic pricing engine for global credit and rates markets. MarketAxess TraX, provides daily
trade volumes and transactional data for more than 42,000 global fixed income instruments. Together,
these datasets provide the market context needed for more efficient liquidity analysis, price discovery,
relative value assessment and risk analytics, without custom integration efforts.

Alex Dobson, SVP and Head of Product at Arcesium, added, “Fixed income markets can be dynamic, one
market movement can have a ripple effect across portfolios. Having more data is only valuable if firms
can lean on market intelligence and operational context across one view in order to make better
decisions. Our integration with MarketAxess provides fixed income teams rich market data and clean
operational data in one place, allowing firms to act on pricing and liquidity signals within their core
operating environment."

Ena Gordon, Head of Data & Analytics Product, at MarketAxess, said: “As fixed income markets grow
more complex, investors need trusted data and purpose-built tools to operate at scale. By integrating our
proprietary data with Arcesium’s platforms, clients can gain a reliable source of truth for fixed income
trading and operations.”

Arcesium has also integrated with MarketAxess Repo Match since June 2024. Through the integration,
Arcesium submits Opterra clients’ repo trades directly to Repo Match for trade-date matching against
counterparty confirmations, including lifecycle events such as re-rates and close-outs. This enhances
efficiency in the repo market by supporting straight through processing, earlier exception resolution and
automated books and records updates. Repo Match connects 127 buy-side and sell-side firms, with over
US$700 billion in matched average daily volume.
 Opterra is a full cloud-native operating platform designed to connect front-, middle-, and back-office
capabilities within a single architecture, bringing precision to all workflows across the entire investment
lifecycle – from position management and reporting to accounting to treasury and reconciliation. It is
tailored to fit the unique operating environments of hedge funds, asset managers, private market funds,
and capital markets firms.

Aquata is a self-service data platform purpose-built for the investment industry, featuring pre-configured
connectivity with data providers, as well as industry-specific data models, lineage, quality, transformation,
and reporting tools. Arcesium Intelligence, embedded in Opterra and Aquata, is designed to empower
firms to deploy agentic AI across investment operations and data management workflows.

About Arcesium

Arcesium© is a global financial technology company delivering front-to-back technology solutions for
some of the world’s most sophisticated financial institutions, including hedge funds, asset managers,
private markets, sell side, and digital assets firms. Expertly designed to achieve a synchronized golden
source of data throughout a client’s ecosystem, Arcesium’s cloud-native technology is built to systematize
the most complex workflows and help clients achieve scale.

Today, Arcesium services over $6.7T in gross AUM and over $1.2T in sell-side capital balances and has
modelled over 178 million investments to date. Arcesium was built from a platform developed and tested
by investment and technology development firm, the D. E. Shaw group, and launched as a joint venture
with Blackstone Multi-Asset Investing. J.P. Morgan, another large client, later made a strategic investment
in the company, helping Arcesium further its mission: to power the entire investment lifecycle. Arcesium
currently has a staff of over 2,600 software engineering, accounting, operations, and treasury
professionals.

For more information about Arcesium and its capabilities, visit www.arcesium.com and follow the firm on
LinkedIn.

About MarketAxess

MarketAxess (Nasdaq: MKTX) operates a leading electronic trading platform that delivers greater trading
efficiency, a diversified pool of liquidity and significant cost savings to institutional investors and broker-
dealers across the global fixed-income markets. Approximately 2,100 firms leverage MarketAxess’
patented technology to efficiently trade fixed-income securities. Our automated and algorithmic trading
solutions, combined with our integrated and actionable data offerings, help our clients make faster, better-
informed decisions on when and how to trade on our platform. MarketAxess’ award-winning Open
Trading® marketplace is widely regarded as the preferred all-to-all trading solution in the global credit
markets. Founded in 2000, MarketAxess connects a robust network of market participants through an
advanced full trading lifecycle solution that includes automated trading solutions, intelligent data and
index products and a range of post-trade services. Learn more at www.marketaxess.com.

title: How AI is transforming fixed income trading | Podcast
text:
How AI is transforming fixed income trading | Podcast
What will it take for autonomous trading agents to become a reality?

In this episode of the Capital Markets FinTech Forum, Gareth Coltman, Head of Product for EMEA & APAC at MarketAxess, joins Matthew Cheung, CEO of ipushpull, to discuss the growing role of AI, machine learning and automation across the fixed income trading lifecycle.

Drawing on more than a decade of innovation at MarketAxess, Gareth explores how data-driven workflows are improving liquidity discovery, counterparty selection and execution outcomes. He also shares his perspective on the rise of generative and agentic AI, the continued importance of voice trading, and why human oversight remains critical as markets move toward greater automation.

From electronification and execution strategy to governance, risk and regulation, the conversation examines how AI is transforming fixed income trading today and where the market could be heading next.

title: IMTC, MarketAxess Enter Relationship to Enhance Liquidity, Scale Custom Fixed Income Portfolios
text:
Integration links IMTC's platform with MarketAxess' global electronic trading network to help institutions trade more efficiently and improve execution quality.
NEW YORK, Sept. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire-PRWeb/ -- IMTC, the fixed income technology platform trusted by buy‑side portfolio managers, today announced an integration with MarketAxess Holdings Inc. (Nasdaq: MKTX), a leading institutional electronic trading platform for global fixed income markets, to enhance liquidity opportunities for market participants.

The integration will allow MarketAxess liquidity to be accessible from IMTC's portfolio and order management workflows. Directly from IMTC's platform, mutual clients can now route orders to MarketAxess and tap into its differentiated liquidity across credit products, all while maintaining rigorous compliance and operational control.

 "By integrating with IMTC's portfolio and order management technology, we are embedding that liquidity directly into the investment workflow, making it easier for our mutual clients to discover opportunities, execute with confidence, and achieve better outcomes." - Spencer Lee, MarketAxess

 Post this

The relationship is designed to:

- Bring MarketAxess' electronic marketplace and liquidity closer to the point of portfolio decision‑making, directly within IMTC's portfolio construction and optimization workflows.

- Support portfolio managers in scaling custom fixed income portfolios, model‑driven strategies and SMAs by linking IMTC's optimization outputs with MarketAxess' electronic trading protocols and diverse liquidity pools.

- Help mutual clients improve execution quality, reduce transaction costs, and streamline end‑to‑end trade workflows from idea generation and portfolio construction through execution and reporting.
FROM MARKETAXESS HEAD OF PRODUCTS, AMERICAS, SPENCER LEE:
"MarketAxess continues to expand the reach of our global network and bring more differentiated liquidity and data to institutional investors. By integrating with IMTC's portfolio and order management technology, we are embedding that liquidity directly into the investment workflow, making it easier for our mutual clients to discover opportunities, execute with confidence, and achieve better outcomes across fixed-income markets."
FROM IMTC CEO RUSSELL FELDMAN:
"As firms look to scale fixed income management, PMs need optimization, compliance, and execution to operate in one connected workflow. Partnering with a leader like MarketAxess allows our mutual clients to tap into a deep liquidity network while turning portfolio decisions into executable orders with greater precision, scale, and auditability."

title: Intercontinental Exchange to Acquire MarketAxess, Creating a Premier Fixed Income Marketplace
text:
Acquisition unites two complementary platforms in global fixed income, connecting institutional and retail investors through one integrated fixed income ecosystem spanning execution, data, indices, and analytics

Clients across more than 90 countries to benefit from deeper liquidity, lower transaction costs, and a seamless end-to-end workflow - from pre-trade analytics through post-trade settlement

Transaction expected to be accretive to adjusted earnings per share (EPS)¹ in the first year

ICE reaffirms plans for ongoing share repurchases

 ATLANTA & NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- 
Intercontinental Exchange, Inc. (NYSE: ICE), one of the world’s leading providers of financial market technology and data powering global capital markets, today announced a definitive agreement to acquire MarketAxess Holdings Inc. (Nasdaq: MKTX), a preeminent electronic trading platform for global institutional fixed income markets. The combination will bring together two highly complementary businesses to form a more complete and connected fixed income platform.
MarketAxess connects approximately 2,100 institutional investors and broker-dealers across more than 90 countries, enabling electronic trading in corporate bonds, municipal bonds, emerging market debt, Eurobonds, U.S. Treasuries, and other fixed income instruments. Together with ICE’s established retail and wealth focused bond trading franchise, deep data and analytics capabilities, and global index business, the combined platform will serve every segment of the fixed income market through a single, unified ecosystem.
Under the terms of the agreement, ICE will acquire all outstanding shares of MarketAxess for $167 per share in cash, representing a 33% premium to MarketAxess’s closing price as of July 29, 2026, representing an equity value of approximately $6.0 billion and a total enterprise value of approximately $5.7 billion. The transaction has been unanimously approved by the Boards of Directors of both companies.
A defining moment for global fixed income markets
The global bond market - with an estimated $145.1 trillion in outstanding debt - has long been one of finance’s most fragmented and opaque areas. Despite decades of progress, fixed income trading remains disproportionately manual, bilateral, and information-asymmetric relative to equities and other asset classes, resulting in lower transparency, wider bid-ask spreads and higher transaction costs. ICE has spent years building the foundational infrastructure to change that: a comprehensive fixed income data and analytics platform, a leading retail bond marketplace, and a global index franchise, aggregating high-quality data to give investors a more complete view of where bonds are trading, where liquidity exists and what a fair price should be. MarketAxess brings the institutional trading network and leading electronic execution capabilities that complete the picture.
The combined company will offer clients a fully integrated workflow spanning pre-trade price discovery and analytics, multi-protocol electronic execution for both retail and institutional investors, and post-trade data, benchmarking, and compliance tools, all within a single connected platform. Traders of fixed income will have access to one global fixed income ecosystem, enabling them to benefit from consolidated liquidity, more competitive pricing, lower operating costs, and a materially improved trading experience.
“For more than two decades, ICE has pursued a clear and consistent strategy: take the largest, least-efficient corners of global finance and apply technology and network effects to improve transparency,” said Jeff Sprecher, ICE Chair and Chief Executive Officer. “That is what we did in energy, in credit default swaps, and in mortgage technology. Acquiring MarketAxess is the natural next step in that journey. Together, we will build the fixed income ecosystem that investors have always deserved - one that is transparent, efficient, fully connected, and accessible to all.”
“This transaction exemplifies the discipline and long-term perspective that define how ICE approaches capital allocation,” said Warren Gardiner, ICE Chief Financial Officer. “We are acquiring a high-quality, cash-generative business and this transaction is expected to be accretive to adjusted EPS¹. Critically, our balance sheet strength allows us to finance this acquisition entirely in cash while maintaining our plans for returning capital to shareholders. We are confident the combination will generate substantial long-term value for ICE shareholders.”
"MarketAxess has built its business by helping solve customer needs in increasingly complex markets," said Chris Concannon, Chief Executive Officer of MarketAxess. "What makes this combination so compelling is the complementary strengths each company brings. MarketAxess contributes a leading fixed-income trading network and deep market expertise, while ICE brings additional retail and wealth trading protocols, strong data, connectivity, and a broader set of product capabilities. Together, we will have the scale to invest more deeply in the areas that matter most to our customers."
Strategic and financial benefits of the combination
Creates a more complete fixed income marketplace. By combining MarketAxess’s deep institutional network with ICE’s retail bond franchise and data infrastructure, the combined platform will serve every category of fixed income participant through a single, unified ecosystem.
Delivers a superior client experience. Clients will benefit from a consolidated liquidity pool, access to richer pre-trade analytics and price discovery, expanded trading protocols, and a seamless end-to-end workflow - translating directly into better execution quality and lower transaction costs.
Accelerates ICE’s data and analytics leadership. MarketAxess’s proprietary trading data and analytics capabilities, combined with ICE’s existing fixed income pricing, reference data, and index business, will create one of the most comprehensive and differentiated fixed income data platforms in the world - a strategic asset of growing importance as passive investing and data-driven decision-making reshape markets.
Key transaction terms
Purchase price of $167 per share in cash, representing a 33% premium to MarketAxess’s closing price as of July 29, 2026, for a total enterprise value of approximately $5.7 billion, or approximately ~10.6x MarketAxess LTM² EBITDA pro forma for full run-rate expense synergies
100% cash consideration financed via newly issued debt (a mix of bonds, term loan and commercial paper)
ICE increases baseline share repurchases to $400 million per quarter from $350 million per quarter. Assumes beginning gross leverage of 3.4x, targeting a return to gross leverage of 3.0x or below within 18 to 24 months post-close, reflecting ICE’s strong balance sheet and free cash flow generation
$100 million in annual run-rate expense synergies, expected to be fully realized within three years post-close
Expected to be accretive to adjusted ICE EPS¹ in the first full year following close
Transaction unanimously approved by the Boards of Directors of both companies; expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to receipt of MarketAxess stockholder approval, applicable regulatory clearances, and customary closing conditions.
BofA Securities is serving as financial advisor to Intercontinental Exchange, and Sullivan & Cromwell LLP and Morgan, Lewis and Bockius LLP are serving as legal advisors to Intercontinental Exchange. J.P. Morgan Securities LLC is serving as financial advisor to MarketAxess and Weil, Gotshal & Manges LLP is serving as legal advisor to MarketAxess.
(1)Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) excludes amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, acquisition and integration expenses and the impact of equity earnings from unconsolidated investees, net of tax.

(2)Last twelve months (LTM) ending June 30, 2026.

(3)Gross leverage figures represent gross debt to pro forma adjusted EBITDA. Pro forma amounts include the combined results of MarketAxess and ICE.

Conference Call Information

A live audio webcast of the conference call will be available on the company's website at www.ice.com in the investor relations section. title: MarketAxess Introduces TraX Tape, Delivering an Enriched View of Bond Market Activity
text:
New data solution enhances usability, transparency and decision-making amid UK and EU transparency reforms

 LONDON--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- 
MarketAxess Holdings Inc. (Nasdaq: MKTX) today announced the launch of TraX® Tape, a data solution that delivers a clean, consolidated view of bond market activity, enriched with additional context and real-time insights.The launch comes as UK and EU transparency reforms increase the availability of bond trading data while adding complexity to how that data is reported and interpreted. TraX Tape addresses these challenges by providing a single, standardised feed that consolidates and enhances market data, enabling clients to interpret trading activity more efficiently and with greater confidence.“Market participants have more data than ever but turning that data into actionable insight remains a challenge,” said Dean Berry, Group COO and CEO of EMEA & APAC at MarketAxess. “TraX Tape is designed to deliver a clearer and more complete view of market activity, helping clients make more informed trading decisions.”Built on MarketAxess TraX data, TraX Tape aggregates data from a global network of dealers and clients and applies proprietary data cleansing processes refined over 10 years. The solution then enriches the regulatory transparency data with additional real-time insights and analytics, including trade direction and pricing context from MarketAxess’ AI-powered pricing engine CP+™.Key features include:Directional indicators on each trade, providing clearer insight into market sentimentA consolidated view of global bond trading activity through a single connectionClean, de-duplicated data to improve usability and reduce operational burdenExpanded coverage and earlier visibility into trading activityIntegrated analytics, including yield and spread calculations, to support trading and execution analysis“The consolidated tape will bring increased transparency and standardisation to global bond markets,” Berry added. “TraX Tape builds upon that foundation and brings clarity with contextual intelligence that can only come from seeing how bonds actually trade on one of the world’s largest electronic credit platforms. The data tells you what happened, and TraX Tape tells you what it means.”About MarketAxessMarketAxess (Nasdaq: MKTX) operates a leading electronic trading platform that delivers greater trading efficiency, a diversified pool of liquidity and significant cost savings to institutional investors and broker-dealers across the global fixed-income and other markets. Approximately 2,100 firms leverage MarketAxess’ patented technology to efficiently trade fixed-income securities. Our automated and algorithmic trading solutions, combined with our integrated and actionable data offerings, help our clients make faster, better-informed decisions on when and how to trade on our platform. MarketAxess’ award-winning Open Trading® marketplace is widely regarded as the preferred all-to-all trading solution in the global credit markets. title: MarketAxess: A better match
text:
MarketAxess: A better match
How is automation in credit markets moving beyond rules-based RFQ execution?
Spencer Lee (SL): For a long time, automation in credit trading meant one thing: making RFQs faster. You’d send a request, apply a set of rules, and auto-execute based on the responses. That’s no longer where the market is. Traders are now able to execute with tools like Adaptive Auto-X™ (ADX), which is a shift towards intelligent orchestration. Orders don’t just follow predefined logic; they’re dynamically routed across protocols to make or take liquidity simultaneously. And importantly, that’s translating into real beneficial outcomes. Clients are executing tens of millions in a day by breaking trades into smaller components and working them across different liquidity and execution sources. Automation isn’t just about efficiency anymore, it’s about expanding what’s achievable.
There’s been a push from some buy-side traders to engage with the market more passively to optimise bid-ask spreads, does that fit with what you’re seeing?
SL: Absolutely. What used to feel like an outlier is becoming part of everyday execution.
Protocols like Live Markets make it possible to passively interact anonymously with both buy- and sell-side liquidity. Posting interest, accessing axes, and allowing the market to come to you. That wasn’t always widely adopted, but the industry is catching up.
Trader mindset has been a catalyst to this shift. They are no longer thinking in terms of which tool to use but instead they’re thinking in terms of how to combine those tools effectively.
That’s where I think the industry still has work to do. As traders are given more protocol options, this also multiplies the number of decisions needed. The real opportunity is to reduce that complexity and streamline that decision-making process. What I’ve long advocated for is a “smart protocol chooser.” Not just routing orders but suggesting how to approach them in the first place, based on data and probability of success. That’s the ideal state.
Beyond axes and algos, how can clients see matching more directly against liquidity in the platform?
SL: The number of liquidity pools available to traders today has grown significantly—client-to-client matching, dealer axes, all-to-all RFQ, workups, auctions , and more.
Individually, none of these protocols are new. What is new is the ability to access them together, in one execution platform, that is where the real advantage lies.
There’s also been renewed interest in concepts like indications of interest (IOIs) to give clients a way to express intent more discreetly while still finding matches. It’s another example of how liquidity provision and liquidity seeking are starting to converge.
What we’re focused on is surfacing those opportunities at the right moment for each trade. Not burying them in a workflow, but making sure traders see high-quality matches when they matter.
Because in this environment, missing the right opportunity is often the biggest risk a trader may face.
Can the matching process itself be improved?
SL: Yes, definitely, and in two significant ways. First, I believe the surface area for matching has to expand materially. This is really about increasing the number of liquidity pools against which buyside orders or IOIs can be cross referenced. Of course, this has to be done with great care to guard against information leakage and then, additionally, we must also improve the hit rates by qualifying the trading interests.
The next step is about moving beyond the individual bond level, towards matching more at the portfolio level that is based on broader risk attributes Historically, trading has been very CUSIP-specific, traders work on one order at a time, a list or portfolio trade of pre-defined cusips. But that doesn’t always reflect how risk is actually managed. Capturing the broader needs of moving bigger blocks of risk can often mean flexibility to accept a number of different cusips to satisfy a particular need, Trading technology has room to grow in this area and it is something that we work as one of the next areas for innovative growth.
At the same time, when you’re working large blocks of orders, you need better ways to control how those orders interact with the market. That’s where the idea of a trading cockpit comes in.
Instead of navigating multiple tools, traders should be able to: adjust aggressiveness dynamically, monitor progress across multiple orders simultaneously, and shift between providing and taking liquidity as conditions change.
It’s less about executing a single trade and more about managing the posture of an entire book of risk.
How does data fit into making that cockpit concept work in practice?
SL: Data is central to this framework but only if it’s actionable. There’s no shortage of information available: continuous pricing, dealer performance, hit rates, historical outcomes. The challenge isn’t access, it’s cutting through the noise in a timely fashion to ascertain relevance.
If that data sits in a report after the fact, it’s not helping the trader. It needs to be there at the point of decision, guiding how an order is worked.
That’s the real opportunity. MarketAxess has various proprietary datasets that are applied across protocols and delivered to traders when they need it most, at the point of trade. The focus now is making sure that insight is embedded directly into the workflow so traders can make better decisions in real time.
If you could redesign buy-side trading desk, what would you change?
SL: I’d simplify it.
Today, traders are navigating multiple protocols, multiple decisions, multiple workflows. But the direction of travel is clear. The most effective desks will treat liquidity provision as a core capability not an occasional tactic, consolidate access to liquidity through a single interface, and use their own trading data alongside market-wide insights to create a continuous feedback loop. Our goal isn’t more tools, it’s better orchestration of them. Ultimately what traders need isn’t more choice, it’s clarity on what to do, when to do it, and why it works.

title: AI won’t replace traders—it will redefine their value
text:
AI won’t replace traders—it will redefine their value
Few topics have dominated industry conversations over the last two years quite like artificial intelligence. Yet after moderating a recent panel discussion with market participants from across the buy side, sell side and technology ecosystem, I came away with a slightly different perspective than the one often reflected in headlines.
For all the discussion about AI transforming financial markets, the most interesting question raised by the panel was not whether AI will replace traders, but where human judgement adds the greatest value. Ironically, the more capable AI becomes, the more important that question may become.
Across the discussion, participants agreed that AI is already creating meaningful value. But not in the way many predicted. Rather than replacing decision-makers, AI is increasingly helping firms access information faster, reduce operational friction and focus expertise where it has the greatest impact.
Beyond efficiency: Where AI is creating value today
One theme emerged consistently throughout the discussion: AI's biggest impact today is not full automation. It is workflow enhancement.
The panel highlighted examples ranging from helping traders classify high-touch and low-touch workflows, to connecting datasets, surfacing relevant information and streamlining decision-making. These are not necessarily the headline-grabbing use cases often associated with AI, but they are delivering tangible value today.
What struck me most was how quickly the conversation moved beyond efficiency. Several panellists argued that as AI reduces the cost of accessing information, competitive advantage increasingly shifts from finding data to interpreting it.
That observation has important implications for fixed income markets. If participants have access to similar technologies and increasingly similar information, differentiation comes less from data retrieval and more from context, experience and risk appetite.
In other words, AI is creating a judgement premium.
The discussion also highlighted how firms are adapting talent strategies in response. We discussed increased investment in trader upskilling, AI training programmes and the integration of technology expertise directly within trading teams. Rather than reducing the importance of people, AI may actually increase the demand for individuals capable of combining market expertise with technical fluency.
This was a point highlighted by Alexandre Guignot, European Head of E-Trading at BNP Paribas, who observed:
"What I haven't seen materialise yet is how we transform the trading desk cockpit and how we make use of those tools, to the full power."
Guignot's comment resonated because it captures where the industry stands today. AI is already delivering meaningful benefits in areas such as price discovery, market making and workflow automation. What remains less clear is how these capabilities ultimately reshape the trader's role and day-to-day workflow.
The panel's answer was largely consistent: the value of the trader increasingly lies not in gathering information, but in understanding what it means.
This was particularly evident in discussions around credit markets, where fragmented liquidity, infrequently traded securities and evolving market conditions create nuances that cannot easily be reduced to a rules-based process. AI can narrow the choices. It can identify patterns. It can surface opportunities and risks. But the final decision still requires judgement.
Generative AI and the future trading workflow
Another recurring theme was how dramatically the arrival of generative AI has changed expectations around technology.
For years, industry conversations focused heavily on data infrastructure, analytics and connectivity. Today, the focus is increasingly on accessibility.
As Andy Mahoney, Managing Director, EMEA at FlexTrade Systems, observed:
"AI has reopened doors for clients to be able to build things on the fly that previously would have taken client service interaction or a coder to do so."
That comment captured one of the most important shifts discussed by the panel. The issue is no longer simply whether firms have access to data. The challenge is how efficiently users can reach it, interrogate it and act on it.
AI is lowering the barrier between people and technology. Tasks that once required specialist coding skills, database knowledge or support teams can increasingly be completed by end users themselves.
Interestingly, this does not mean traditional trading tools are disappearing. The discussion highlighted that traders still value familiar interfaces for monitoring markets and executing trades. Where AI is delivering the greatest value is in bringing together information from multiple sources and helping users perform complex tasks that previously required significant manual effort.
The evolution resembles a shift from integrated platforms to connected ecosystems. Just as consumers move seamlessly between specialised applications on their phones, trading workflows could increasingly be assembled from interoperable services, data sources and execution tools linked through APIs. This is consistent with a broader industry push towards creating a more data-rich, user-friendly environment across the trade lifecycle.
Several panellists suggested that APIs are increasingly moving from connectivity tools to strategic infrastructure, enabling firms to build their own workflows, decision layers and user experiences around a common set of services and data.
Trust: The foundation of AI adoption
A recurring tension throughout the discussion centred on trust.
Beneath the conversations about AI, automation and APIs sat a more fundamental question: how confident are we in the decisions being made?
As Max Callaghan, Head of Sales EMEA at MarketAxess, put it:
"Trust and communication is very commercially challenging."
That insight resonated because it extends far beyond AI.
AI requires trust. Electronic markets require trust. Data requires trust. Execution quality requires trust.
The more decision-making becomes data-driven, the more important data quality becomes. AI can accelerate analysis, but it cannot compensate for incomplete, inconsistent or misleading inputs. Several panellists highlighted challenges around dealer selection, market signalling and execution quality, questioning whether increasing transparency and richer performance data may ultimately prove more valuable than traditional liquidity signals alone.
What became clear during the discussion is that firms are unlikely to automate critical decisions simply because they can. They will automate them when they trust the underlying data, understand how decisions are being made and have confidence in the outcomes being generated.
Trust is not a barrier to adoption. It is the prerequisite.
Looking ahead
A final observation stayed with me after the panel concluded.
The fixed income industry has always adopted technology to make markets more efficient, transparent and accessible. AI represents the next chapter of that evolution. But its greatest impact may not be replacing judgement. It may be making judgement more valuable than ever.
As information becomes more abundant and more accessible, the differentiator is unlikely to be who has the most data or even the most automation. It will be who can best combine technology, experience and context to make better decisions.
The winners will not simply be the firms that automate the most. They will be the firms that pair powerful technology with the insight, judgement and trust that remain distinctly human. That, more than any prediction about autonomous trading, was the strongest conclusion I took away from the panel discussion.

title: How US regulation can support evolving fixed income market structure
text:
How US regulation can support evolving fixed income market structure
The following piece is a compilation of takeaways from our team based on discussions at the recent US FILS conference, where regulatory change and shifting market dynamics were leading topics.
Highlights

- Multi-protocol electronic trading is reshaping execution choice and reinforcing the need for a modern best execution framework.

- Richer data and streaming prices are enabling greater buy-side participation in price formation, challenging rules designed for traditional liquidity providers.

- Public and private credit convergence is driving demand for consistent pricing, valuation and disclosure frameworks.

- Derivatives, tokenization and AI are testing regulatory boundaries and reinforcing the need for strong investor protection.

- Targeted regulatory updates can reduce friction and improve efficiency while preserving market integrity.

Technology and structural innovation have expanded what is possible in fixed income for the buy-side. Electronic trading, richer data and greater visibility are enabling asset managers, institutional investors and hedge funds to transform from price-taking, buy-and-hold investors into proactive liquidity providers.
With daily fixed income trading volumes roughly twice those of equities, performance is consequential, and regulation is taking a more active part in the conversation. US policymakers are examining a wide range of issues, from Treasury clearing and private credit to transparency requirements and emerging technologies. The regulatory task is to stay at pace with evolution, focusing on targeted interventions that remove friction and improve outcomes where it matters most.
The question for the buy side is: where can regulation evolve to support more efficient, transparent and resilient fixed income markets?
In support of the price-making investor
The buy side has historically played the role of price taker rather than price maker in fixed income. Institutional investors today use limit orders in approximately 70% of equity trading activity, actively contributing prices. In fixed income, however, that figure remains below 5%, indicating minimal price making.
To help bring more buy-side firms directly into the pricing process, both the US Treasury and the SEC have encouraged all-to-all protocols that broaden participation in liquidity provision, particularly in less liquid conditions. Continued support for these models will be important as the market evolves.
At MarketAxess, in addition to the use of our Open Trading all-to-all protocol, we are seeing some sizeable institutional investors use our pricing tools and data to express prices directly. A key driver behind this trend is that price is becoming data. Real-time feeds and continuous data consumption are now common in credit, providing an infrastructure to assess value, evaluate liquidity, and contribute prices. Investors who can see conditions more clearly are better positioned to participate in it more actively.
Best execution frameworks need to reflect a multi-protocol environment
Today's fixed income landscape spans portfolio trading, RFQ, all-to-all trading and single-dealer workflows, each playing a distinct role in liquidity access. That breadth of choice is changing how buy-side firms pursue and demonstrate best execution as part of their overarching fiduciary duties. Existing regulatory frameworks were built around a dealer-centric RFQ model, where outcomes were assessed through a relatively narrow set of price comparisons and dealer interactions. In a multi-protocol environment, execution quality is shaped by streaming prices, trade analytics, and highly distributed liquidity sources.
As market data becomes more embedded in execution workflows, best execution is becoming more measurable and more data-driven. This creates an opportunity to revisit how execution quality is assessed and evidenced, so that regulatory standards better reflect the tools, data and execution protocols available to buy-side traders today.
Affiliate cross rule modernization could reduce unnecessary costs
Affiliate cross rules are a clear example of where legacy structure no longer matches reality.
Many asset managers operate multiple funds with different investment mandates. When a bond is downgraded from investment grade to high yield, current requirements force those transactions out into the open market, even though they could simply be moved to another fund within the same complex. This can increase trading costs and operational complexity, with firms effectively paying the spread twice despite the availability of pricing data and valuation tools that could support fair internal crosses.
Affiliate cross modernization is a high-impact, targeted change that could materially reduce transaction costs while using the transparency and pricing infrastructure that already exists.
Public and private credit convergence
Private credit has grown into a major asset class, with many buy-side trading desks now managing both public and private credit exposures. The two segments are converging through investment vehicles such as ETFs and closed-end funds that incorporate private assets alongside publicly traded securities.
Industry participants and regulators are focused on developing appropriate frameworks for pricing private assets, determining valuation frequency and disclosing holdings in ways that protect investors while supporting broader access to private assets.
The municipal bond sector offers a useful parallel. Although many municipal securities trade infrequently and can be difficult to value, we have developed robust pricing methodologies that support trading and investment activity. Similar advances in data, pricing models, public-market proxies and arbitrage relationships could help address transparency and valuation challenges in private credit.
For regulators, the opportunity is to enable consistent disclosure and scalable pricing frameworks that support integration across public and private markets without constraining product development.
Defining regulatory boundaries for new product innovations
Recent developments in derivatives, such as the approval of bitcoin perpetual futures, have intensified discussion around how far these structures could extend into broader capital markets, including fixed income.
Fixed income is fundamentally different from crypto in its role as core instruments for savings, funding and portfolio construction. Extending similar instruments into securities-linked products would raise important questions about leverage, suitability and retail participation.
The core issue is retail exposure. Highly leveraged, continuously funded products sit uncomfortably close to gambling-style behavior when combined with 24/7 access and seamless distribution. That creates a clear regulatory fault line around suitability and investor protection.
Regulation should ensure that innovation in product design does not move ahead of the protections that underpin investor confidence and market integrity.
AI is accelerating innovation while testing existing regulatory frameworks
AI is being embedded across fixed income trading and investment workflows, enabling new opportunities for automation, analysis and decision support. Regulators are becoming more comfortable with certain applications where firms can clearly explain how the technology operates and how outcomes are governed.
With the use of AI moving closer to investment recommendations and client-facing activities, questions are emerging around accountability and fiduciary responsibility. Regulators and industry participants alike should assess how established standards of care and oversight apply.
Firms adopting AI must ensure sensitive, proprietary and material non-public information is appropriately protected. The tools may be evolving, but expectations around data protection, confidentiality and responsible use should continue to apply.
Looking ahead
As fixed income evolves, regulation has to stay focused on what actually moves outcomes. The most effective regulatory updates are targeted and practical: modernized best execution standards, sensible reforms to the affiliate cross rule and continued support for buy-side participation in price formation. The goal is to keep friction out of the parts of the system where it no longer serves a purpose, and stay firm where investor protection depends on it.

title: Repo reinvented: how speed, clarity and confidence are reshaping the future of repo markets
text:
Repo reinvented: how speed, clarity and confidence are reshaping the future of repo markets
Volumes are higher than ever, participation is broader, and regulatory change is compressing timelines across the trade lifecycle. The next chapter of repo will be shaped by infrastructure, operating models, and the industry’s ability to deliver speed alongside clarity and confidence.
A market moving faster with less tolerance for friction
Repo markets today operate at a scale and velocity that would have been difficult to imagine even a decade ago. Macroeconomic volatility, shifts in monetary policy, and changes in the composition of market participants have driven sustained growth in activity. At the same time, regulatory initiatives — notably the move to T+1 settlement in Europe and the UK, and mandatory clearing in the United States — are going to compress already tight operational timelines even further.
Historically, repo infrastructure evolved to solve the problems of its time, with longer settlement cycles, overnight batch processing, and relationship-driven workflows. Many of today’s processes, such as manual exception handling and bespoke data formats, are rational adaptations to those earlier constraints.
In a T+1 environment, however, those adaptations are exposed as sources of risk. Speed is now a baseline requirement. Firms must effectively manage the trade lifecycle end-to-end: from execution through confirmation, allocation, lifecycle events, settlement and, increasingly, clearing. Faster markets leave less room for ambiguity: inconsistent data or unclear ownership quickly turns into operational risk.
Data consistency as the foundation of clarity
One of the most persistent challenges in repo remains data inconsistency. Different booking models, system representations, and message formats still describe the same economic trade in subtly different ways. These inconsistencies are a primary driver of exceptions, manual intervention, and delayed settlement.
For years, the repo industry has attempted to address this through standardisation, often by imposing rigid data requirements on participants. While standards remain important, experience has shown that inflexibility can create new barriers, particularly for firms with constrained technology resources.
A growing consensus is therefore emerging around a different approach: normalisation at the point of ingestion. By accepting trade data in multiple formats and transforming it centrally, market infrastructure can reduce integration friction while preserving consistency downstream. The result is fewer exceptions, faster onboarding, and greater scalability.
This clarity has important implications for market structure. As participation expands beyond traditional dealer banks, lowering technical barriers becomes essential. Data normalisation and clarity become enablers of broader, more resilient participation.
Beyond trade matching: clarity across the trade lifecycle
As settlement cycles compress, the limitations of a narrow focus on trade matching become increasingly apparent. Matching alone does not guarantee settlement. Trades must navigate a complex series of downstream processes, often involving multiple systems and teams.
Participants consistently highlighted the need for holistic lifecycle visibility that includes a single, coherent view of where each trade sits, what events have occurred, and what remains outstanding. Today, that information is frequently fragmented across confirmation platforms, settlement systems, custodians, and clearing workflows.
During periods of market stress, uncertainty about trade status can amplify risk far more quickly than price movements themselves. In such environments, clarity becomes a form of resilience.
Bringing settlement status, lifecycle events, allocation flows and clearing parameters into a unified operational view allows firms to prioritise effectively and reduce the likelihood of cascading failures. It also shifts the role of operations from reactive problem-solving to proactive risk management.
Automation driving confidence
Automation has long been part of the repo narrative, but its focus is changing.
Areas such as pair-offs, allocations, and lifecycle event processing have remained highly manual, often requiring repeated intervention across both sides of a trade. These processes are now being redesigned to support configuration-driven automation, where rules are defined once and applied consistently at scale.
Automation supports a faster settlement environment by delivering speed and greater confidence in predictable outcomes and auditability.
The practical role of artificial intelligence
Artificial intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of repo, but in a notably pragmatic way. The emphasis was not on replacing human judgment, but on enhancing it.
By analysing historical matching behaviour, counterparty patterns and market context, AI-driven tools can help identify the most likely causes of exceptions, suggest corrective actions, and prioritise issues that genuinely threaten settlement. In doing so, they allow operations teams to concentrate their efforts more effectively.
AI also offers a powerful lever in onboarding and integration. Mapping data fields between systems has traditionally been a time-consuming, manual exercise, often taking months. Early evidence suggests that AI-assisted mapping can dramatically accelerate this process, reducing time-to-connect and supporting faster market expansion.
Regulation as a catalyst for structural change
Regulatory change has long been one of the most powerful forces shaping repo markets, and the current cycle is no exception. T+1 settlement and clearing mandates are forcing firms to confront long-standing structural issues.
Fragmented ownership across trading, treasury, collateral and operations functions remains common. Investment has historically prioritised front-office capability over post-trade resilience. In many organisations, processes have been layered rather than redesigned.
The risk, as several participants observed, is that firms respond to regulatory change by doing the minimum required to comply. The opportunity lies in treating regulation as a moment to rearchitect operating models for a faster, more resilient future.
Central clearing illustrates this dynamic particularly clearly. Mandatory clearing introduces new workflows, data requirements, and connectivity points, often without a single prescribed industry model. Supporting broader access, including sponsored clearing for non-banks, requires infrastructure that can deliver transparency and scale without increasing operational burden.
The buy-side perspective: transparency and predictability
The growing role of buy-side participants has fundamentally changed the dynamics of repo markets. Hedge funds, asset managers, and pension schemes are no longer peripheral users; they are core participants with distinct needs and expectations.
Across discussions, buy-side priorities were strikingly consistent. They seek transparency into where trades sit in the lifecycle, confidence through predictable settlement outcomes, and operating models that allow them to access liquidity without disproportionate complexity.
These demands reinforce the importance of clarity through lifecycle visibility and intelligent automation. As participation broadens, infrastructure must accommodate diverse operating models while maintaining consistency and control. Confidence, for the buy side, is inseparable from clarity.
Reimagining repo
Repo has reinvented itself before, often in response to external pressure. The current reinvention is no different in that regard, but it is broader in scope. It touches every part of the lifecycle and every category of participant.
What is changing is not just how fast repo markets operate, but how clearly they operate. As speed increases, clarity becomes essential. As participation broadens, confidence becomes the foundation of growth.
The discussions in London made clear that the industry understands both the challenge and the opportunity. The next era of repo will be built on a renewed focus on infrastructure, data and operating models that support speed, clarity and confidence.
That reinvention is already underway.

title: MarketAxess and Moment Partner to Provide Retail Access to Institutional Fixed-Income Liquidity
text:

MarketAxess Holdings Inc.
