title: 2025 Annual Report: Letter to Stockholders and Clients (Christopher Concannon)
text:
25 Proxy Statement and Notice of Annual Meeting of Stockholders
  Dear Fellow Stockholders and Clients,
In 2025, we made significant strides in enhancing the “MarketAxess advantage” by expanding our leading
global network, deepening our differentiated liquidity and accelerating our use of artificial intelligence
(“AI”) to strengthen our proprietary data and analytics. These key components of our “advantage” were
further complemented by our investments in multi-protocol solutions for our clients.
Delivering record financial and operating performance
The market backdrop in 2025 was characterized by continued tight credit spreads and low credit spread
volatility, short periods of event-driven volatility and another year of strong new issuance. With yields
remaining elevated, fixed income continued to be an attractive asset class in 2025, and MarketAxess
played a leading role in providing liquidity and enabling price discovery.
Our global network had over 2,100 active client firms at the end of 2025, including over 1,000 active
international client firms and close to 13,000 active traders, approximately half of which were located
outside of the United States. This global network is at the core of our differentiated liquidity, with over
1,000 unique liquidity providers on Open Trading, where alternative liquidity providers like hedge funds
and systematics are increasingly playing a key role. Our differentiated liquidity depends on our proprietary
data and analytics, powered by CP+. In 2025, our clients submitted $5.3 trillion in notional inquiries and
received over 440 million responses. This activity is among the reasons our CP+ data is so robust.
The work that we have done to solidify our competitive advantage in the global credit markets helped us
generate a record $846 million in revenue in 2025—our 17th consecutive year of record annual revenue—
on total trading volume of $10.5 trillion, representing a 13% year-over-year increase in trading volume.
These results were driven by strong growth and record trading volumes across most of our product areas.
In emerging markets, one of our most promising future growth drivers, we surpassed $1 trillion in trading
volume in 2025 for the first time, driven by strong growth across both hard currency and local currency
markets.1
Driving increased revenue and market share across our three main strategic channels
We believe that the new protocols and workflow tools that we launched in 2025 will position us to drive
U.S. credit revenue growth across the client-initiated, portfolio trading and dealer-initiated channels.
 In our leading client-initiated channel, we launched our targeted block trading solution for U.S.
 credit, emerging markets and eurobonds. This is an exciting new initiative, as it will enable us to
 further electronify one of the most valuable segments of our total addressable market in U.S.
 credit. Total block trading average daily volume (“ADV”) increased 24% to a record $5 billion,
 including record growth of 18% in U.S. credit, 27% in emerging markets and 66% in eurobonds.
 In the portfolio trading channel, our enhanced portfolio trading solution in X-Pro is increasingly
 being leveraged by our clients. Our estimated market share in U.S. credit portfolio trading in 2025
 was 19.0%, an increase of 270 basis points over our full-year 2024 estimated market share.
 In the dealer-initiated channel, we expanded our dealer solutions suite and enhanced our
 sessions-based trading protocol, Mid-X, in U.S. credit. We continue to broaden dealer
 participation and increase the number of trading sessions per day.

 1
 We have a clear and achievable technology and product roadmap to drive U.S. credit revenue growth
across these three channels which we believe will be integral to achieving the financial targets2 we
announced at the end of 2025.
Introduction of medium-term financial targets2 and enhanced capital return plan
Over the last several years, we have made significant progress on our technology transformation and
investments in innovative protocols and workflow tools. We still have work to do, but based on our three-
year technology and product roadmap, we announced medium-term financial targets and an enhanced
capital return plan, which included a $400 million3stock repurchase authorization. Utilizing the new
authorization, MarketAxess executed a $300 million accelerated stock repurchase (“ASR”) program that
settled in February 2026.4 The announcement of the targets and the enhanced capital return plan are
reflections of the Board’s confidence in our long-term strategy and commitment to drive stockholder
value creation. The three-year medium-term financial targets (2026-2028) are as follows:

One of the key imperatives for achieving these medium-term financial targets, is a return to higher levels
of revenue in U.S. credit driven by our new initiatives across the three strategic channels discussed earlier.
Strengthening our franchise with focus on automation, services, strategic partnerships and investments
We continue to experience strong demand for our trading automation solutions, with a record 261 active
clients leveraging our tools. Automation trading volume increased 15% in 2025 and represented a record
28% of total credit trade count and a record 11% of total credit trading volume. We believe that as clients
increasingly leverage automation, our platform becomes more deeply integrated into their trading
workflows. We are also pleased to see our clients increasingly leveraging automation for larger sized
trades.
Beyond our core commission-based trading products, we also delivered record services revenue of $112
million, which includes our information services, post-trade services and technology services businesses.
We believe that these services complement our trading technologies and further our mission to create an
intelligent global electronic fixed-income marketplace that works better for everyone.
In 2025 and early 2026, we announced new partnerships, strategic investments and new protocols,
including:
 The closing of the acquisition of majority control of RFQ-hub Holdings LLC, a bilateral multi-asset
 and multi-dealer request for quote platform designed for the exchange traded fund and
 derivatives markets;
 Growing our EM offering by becoming the first platform to provide fully electronic workflow for
 the trading of Indian Government Bonds to international investors;
 The launch of the fixed income market’s first closing auctions protocol designed to improve
 pricing and liquidity; and
 Most recently, our upcoming announced integration with DirectBooks to streamline access to
 primary issuance data for mutual clients.

 2
 New Board members and new additions to our leadership team
In early 2025, we welcomed Roberto Hoornweg to our Board, who brings extensive global financial
markets expertise, fixed-income knowledge and leadership experience from senior roles at Standard
Chartered, Brevan Howard and Morgan Stanley. More recently, in March 2026, we were very pleased to
add Douglas Cifu and Kenneth Schiciano as new Board members. Doug brings deep fintech and regulatory
expertise from building a major global market maker, while Ken contributes more than three decades of
financial technology and private equity experience from a leading global investment firm.
We also welcomed several key leaders to our management team, including Dean Berry as Group COO and
CEO of EMEA & APAC, and Spencer Lee as Head of Client Products, Americas. Dean joined from LSEG and
brings deep expertise in managing trading workflows and analytics and has a consistent record of scaling
businesses profitably through technology and product transformation. Spencer brings tremendous fixed-
income and market structure expertise to us and his buy-side perspective will be invaluable as we continue
to develop innovative protocols and workflow tools for our clients.
Finally, to further advance our technology transformation, William Quan joined us as Chief Technology
Officer in March 2026. William’s mandate is to drive innovation, support our ongoing modernization
efforts and strengthen technology execution across the enterprise.
Looking forward
I am encouraged by the products and protocols we launched in 2025 and the progress we achieved across
our strategic channels. The investments we are making to drive continued revenue growth are beginning
to gain traction and position us for stronger momentum ahead.
The macro backdrop for fixed-income markets remains attractive. Strong new issuance in 2025 continued
into the first quarter of 2026, supported by strong inflows into U.S. credit, increased velocity of trading in
U.S. high-grade and a modest ease in interest rates. We believe MarketAxess is well positioned to support
our clients through evolving market conditions, including the heightened credit market volatility driven
by the geopolitical backdrop.
We have made tremendous headway over the last several years, and I am confident in the strategy we
have put in place to pursue our financial targets for 2026 – 2028.
I would like to thank our stockholders for their partnership and our Board of Directors for their guidance
in driving the growth of our company. Most importantly, I would like to thank all MarketAxess employees
for their dedication to delivering results for our clients and stockholders.

Sincerely,

Christopher Concannon
Chief Executive Officer
April 29, 2026

title: William Quan to Join MarketAxess as Chief Technology Officer
text:
NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- 
MarketAxess Holdings Inc. (Nasdaq: MKTX), the operator of a leading electronic trading platform for fixed income securities, today announced that William Quan will join MarketAxess as Chief Technology Officer.In this role, Mr. Quan will lead the company’s global Technology organization with a mandate to advance innovation, support ongoing technology modernization, and strengthen execution across the enterprise. He will focus on building modern, resilient, and scalable platforms, setting high engineering standards and implementing AI and advanced data capabilities across MarketAxess.“William brings deep technical expertise and a strong execution mindset that will help us accelerate platform modernization and more deeply embed AI and advanced analytics across our products and workflows,” said Dean Berry, Chief Operating Officer of MarketAxess. “His leadership will be instrumental as we continue to build intelligent, product-led solutions that enable our clients to trade more efficiently and confidently in increasingly complex markets.”Mr. Quan brings more than two decades of global experience leading technology, AI, and digital transformation across financial services and platform businesses. Most recently, he served as Chief Technology Officer of Fleete Group, a Macquarie Asset Management portfolio company, where he led the development of an AI-enabled SaaS platform and a global engineering organization. Previously, he held senior technology leadership roles at Amazon Web Services, advising global financial institutions on cloud-native and AI-driven platforms. Prior to that, he spent over a decade at J.P. Morgan and Deutsche Bank leading electronic trading, AI, and digital platform initiatives across global markets.“I am delighted to be joining MarketAxess and partnering with customers across the dealer and investor community,” said William Quan. “As fixed-income markets continue to expand across electronic trading and distribution channels, there is a compelling opportunity to advance product‑led innovation supported by leading technology capabilities. This focus will drive the delivery of efficient, high‑quality customer solutions across pricing, execution, and intelligent workflows enhanced by AI and advanced data analytics.”As Chief Technology Officer, Mr. Quan will join the Company’s Executive Committee and report directly to Dean Berry.About MarketAxessMarketAxess (Nasdaq: MKTX) operates a leading electronic trading platform that delivers greater trading efficiency, a diversified pool of liquidity and significant cost savings to institutional investors and broker-dealers across the global fixed-income and other markets. Approximately 2,100 firms leverage MarketAxess’ patented technology to efficiently trade fixed-income securities. Founded in 2000, MarketAxess connects a robust network of market participants through an advanced full trading lifecycle solution that includes automated trading solutions, intelligent data and index products and a range of post-trade services. title: MarketAxess and DirectBooks Announce Integration to Streamline Access to Primary Issuance Data
text:
NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- MarketAxess Holdings Inc. (Nasdaq: MKTX), the operator of a leading electronic trading platform for fixed-income securities and DirectBooks, the capital markets platform focused on optimizing global financing markets, today announced an agreement to provide mutual clients with streamlined access to DirectBooks’ primary issuance information and workflow tools through a new MarketAxess integration.
For the first time, mutual clients of DirectBooks and MarketAxess will be able to manage their primary processes through a separate interface on MarketAxess, increasing workflow efficiency and access for buy-side traders. The integration allows MarketAxess clients to review DirectBooks deal announcements, submit indications of interest, and receive allocation messages from syndicate desks, providing increased speed, accuracy, and transparency across the deal lifecycle.
“DirectBooks is delighted to welcome MarketAxess as our newest connectivity partner,” said Rich Kerschner, Chief Executive Officer of DirectBooks. “We are committed to enhancing efficiency across the primary markets for all counterparties. Integrating with MarketAxess was a natural choice given their scale, technology leadership, and deep client network in global fixed income.”
“We are excited to be working with DirectBooks to solve our clients’ workflow and data challenges across the entire lifecycle of a corporate bond,” said Chris Concannon, Chief Executive Officer of MarketAxess. “This integration not only delivers high quality structured data and connectivity to our clients but also streamlined access to the primary issuance process.”
The integration will be available to mutual clients in Q2.
About MarketAxess
MarketAxess (Nasdaq: MKTX) operates a leading electronic trading platform that delivers greater trading efficiency, a diversified pool of liquidity and significant cost savings to institutional investors and broker-dealers across the global fixed-income markets. Approximately 2,100 firms leverage MarketAxess’ patented technology to efficiently trade fixed-income securities. Our automated and algorithmic trading solutions, combined with our integrated and actionable data offerings, help our clients make faster, better-informed decisions on when and how to trade on our platform. MarketAxess’ award-winning Open Trading® marketplace is widely regarded as the preferred all-to-all trading solution in the global credit markets. Founded in 2000, MarketAxess connects a robust network of market participants through an advanced full trading lifecycle solution that includes automated trading solutions, intelligent data and index products and a range of post-trade services. Learn more at www.marketaxess.com and on X @MarketAxess.
About DirectBooks
DirectBooks leverages its technology expertise and market knowledge to optimize global financing markets. We are simplifying the primary issuance process for fixed income by streamlining communications workflows for underwriters and institutional investors. DirectBooks ownership consists of Bank of America, Barclays, BNP Paribas, Citi, Deutsche Bank, Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Mizuho, Royal Bank of Canada, and Wells Fargo. A complete list of participating underwriting firms can be found on our website. For additional information, please visit us: www.DirectBooks.com

We define EBITDA margin as EBITDA divided by revenues. We define free cash flow as net cash provided by/(used in) operating activities excluding the net change in trading investments and net change in securities failed-to-deliver and securities failed-to-receive from broker-dealers, clearing organizations and customers, less expenditures for furniture, equipment and leasehold improvements and capitalized software development costs. Non-GAAP financial measures should be considered in addition to, not as a substitute for or superior to, financial measures determined in conformity with GAAP. title: AI in fixed income: from fragmentation to intelligent execution
text:
AI in fixed income: from fragmentation to intelligent execution
MarketAxess is integrating artificial intelligence across pricing, liquidity discovery and execution workflows to help clients navigate fragmented fixed income markets. Combining proprietary trading data, advanced analytics and electronic trading infrastructure, the firm is helping shape the next generation of intelligent fixed income trading.
For decades, fixed income markets have been defined by fragmentation, opacity, and human intermediation. Unlike equities, where centralized order books provide continuous price discovery and relatively standardized execution, credit and emerging markets remain largely over-the-counter (OTC) ecosystems in which liquidity is dispersed, and pricing must be inferred rather than observed.
Artificial intelligence is beginning to change that structure, not by removing complexity, but by making it legible.
The irony is that fixed income’s historical inefficiencies are precisely what makes it such fertile ground for machine learning. Where prices are not directly observable, liquidity is fragmented across dealers, and the same instrument may trade at different levels depending on size or counterparty, AI has a structural advantage: it can synthesize partial signals into coherent estimates of market reality.
This article explores how:

- AI is moving from experimentation to infrastructure in fixed income: adoption is broad and increasingly embedded across workflows, not confined to isolated pilots.

- The most valuable current applications are pre‑trade pricing intelligence, liquidity sourcing and targeting, and execution—areas where fixed income’s fragmentation makes human-only interpretation difficult at scale.

- The differentiator is in high-quality, permissioned data and workflow integration, plus clear human control and governance. Outputs are explainable, controllable, and operational in real trading decisions.

From inference to algorithmic pricing intelligence
Nearly a decade ago, machine learning began to play a foundational role in early pricing models. These models demonstrated that fragmented OTC data could be transformed into usable signals, enabling better price discovery, more efficient execution, and more sophisticated liquidity provision strategies. Over time, this capability has evolved into more advanced infrastructure, including AI-driven pricing engines like CP+™ that combine public trade prints, proprietary transaction data, dealer responses to inquiries, and even non-executed “intent” signals from across the trading network.
A critical insight underpinning these systems is that information does not only reside in trades that happen, but also in trades that do not. Dealer responses, quoted levels, and patterns of engagement all contribute to a richer representation of market conditions. Machine learning models, when properly calibrated, can extract meaning from this broader informational layer, improving both transaction cost analysis and forward-looking price formation.
AI at the core of the trading workflow
At the same time, AI is increasingly being embedded not only in pricing but also directly into the trading workflow itself. One of the most significant shifts is occurring at the point of counterparty selection. Rather than relying solely on intuition, relationships, or static analytics, tools such as AI Select can evaluate dozens of dynamic variables to recommend the liquidity providers most likely to deliver a strong outcome. These include historical win rates, execution quality, responsiveness, and time-varying behavioral patterns. Models like Tradability use machine learning to estimate likely market depth at the bond, side, and size level, helping traders better anticipate liquidity conditions before initiating a request-for-quote.
Used alongside dealer axes, these systems help traders identify where liquidity is both most credible and most actionable, particularly in situations where a counterparty is simultaneously signaling interest and algorithmically surfaced as a strong execution partner.
This evolution is accompanied by new protocols designed to improve pre-trade information flow while reducing signaling risk. Time-limited “live axe” mechanisms, for example, allow dealers to publish actionable liquidity indications with greater precision and control, enhancing transparency while helping manage signaling risk.
The next stage will likely be defined by natural language interfaces that are deeply grounded in permissioned market data and embedded directly into trading workflows. Their value would move beyond simple conversational access to the ability to ask domain-specific questions—about recent prints, liquidity conditions, counterparty behavior, or execution strategies—and receive answers that are traceable, contextual, and actionable.
Collapsing the boundary between “what” and “how” to trade
The use of AI in fixed income is creating a deeper structural change in how decisions are made. Historically, fixed income workflows separated “what to trade” from “how to trade it,” with portfolio construction and execution treated as distinct problems. AI is beginning to narrow that separation. Investment intent and execution strategy are being considered together, with liquidity conditions, execution constraints, and counterparty behavior feeding back into portfolio design rather than being treated only as downstream execution considerations.
This is particularly relevant in portfolio trading, where execution quality is highly sensitive to size and composition. While portfolio trading can deliver strong outcomes, execution quality can become more sensitive as portfolio size, complexity, or liquidity dispersion increases. AI-enabled optimization allows these larger portfolios to be restructured into smaller, more digestible components, improving execution efficiency by aligning each basket with the most appropriate liquidity providers.
The block trade frontier
As more routine flow becomes automated and electronically intermediated, trader attention and balance sheet engagement can be focused more deliberately on complex transactions. In that sense, efficiency in smaller trades can support better handling of larger block trades, which remain among the least electronified segments of fixed income markets.
Even here, however, AI is beginning to play a role. Rather than attempting full automation, its impact is emerging through better counterparty targeting, improved request-for-quote distribution, and enhanced understanding of liquidity availability. By ensuring that large trades are directed only toward the most relevant counterparties, market impact can be reduced while execution quality improves.
Agentic AI and the question of control
Across all of these developments, a consistent distinction emerges between traditional algorithmic trading systems and newer agentic AI approaches. Conventional execution algorithms are typically rule-based, deterministic, and extensively backtested prior to deployment. By contrast, agentic systems are more adaptive: they can reason across broader datasets, respond to changing market context, and support more dynamic decision workflows. Therefore, an immediate opportunity for agentic AI is likely upstream of live execution, in areas such as data analysis and signal generation.
This flexibility, however, introduces new requirements. Unlike static models, adaptive systems cannot rely solely on historical validation. They require continuous oversight, rigorous governance frameworks, and, critically, a human-in-the-loop approach to ensure that flexibility does not compromise control.
From experimentation to infrastructure
As fixed income markets continue the transition towards the adoption of AI across trading workflows, the relationship between platform providers and clients is evolving. Market participants are building their own AI tools and combining them with external data and execution capabilities. The result is a hybrid model in which proprietary client systems and platform infrastructure interact to produce more sophisticated decision-making environments. Value is no longer concentrated in a single layer, but at the intersection of internal and external intelligence.
What becomes clear across all these developments is that AI is not simply accelerating existing processes. It is changing the structure of how fixed income markets process information. The traditional separation between data, decision, and execution is being replaced by a more continuous system in which information is constantly interpreted, refined, and acted upon.
As AI becomes more deeply embedded in market structure, competitive advantage will belong to firms that can translate complex market activity into scalable trading insight.
At MarketAxess, we are leading that evolution. The use of AI is embedded across our trading and workflow infrastructure, enabling clients to navigate fixed income markets with greater precision, efficiency and confidence. By combining one of the industry’s deepest pools of proprietary trading and workflow data with advanced analytics and electronic trading capabilities, we are transforming the future of fixed income trading.

title: Axe quality in electronic credit markets: What the data tells us
text:
Axe quality in electronic credit markets: What the data tells us
Axe quality has become one of the more energetically debated topics in electronic fixed income, and it was a pleasure to be part of the FIX panel exploring it with Byron Cooper-Fogarty of Neptune Networks Ltd, Mike Roffey of Tradeweb, and Ricardo Goddard of Schroders, chaired by Matthew Coupe of Susquehanna, and the broader community. These are important conversations, and they are most productive when grounded in shared data.
This note sets out how we at MarketAxess think about axe quality: how we define it, what we measure, and what we are building to keep standards high. It is not intended as a defence of any particular position, but as a transparent account of what our data shows and where we think the industry can continue to improve together.
Measuring axe quality through outcomes
There are a number of measures the market participants use to determine whether an axe is an authoritative signal in clients’ decision-making process. We have generally found it useful to anchor our research in outcomes: does the dealer respond when inquired? Do they stand firm at the levels they posted? Are their prices competitive relative to non-axed alternatives? These items are measurable, and they give us a consistent basis for assessment. By these standards, a high-quality axe is one that is current, responsive, and aggressive relative to the market at the time of inquiry.
A broadly healthy ecosystem
Looking at EUR IG, which represents the most mature axe ecosystem across the markets we operate in, the headline metrics are encouraging. Axed dealers, as a community, consistently outperform their non-axed counterparts across standard measures—responsiveness, slippage (improvement), and aggressiveness.
Today, axed dealers win 48% of all inquiries in EUR IG, and on average, an axed dealer has around 2x higher responsiveness compared to non-axed dealers and has close to 3x higher win rates when participating in the same inquiry, as we demonstrated here. These are meaningful differentials, and they have been stable or improving over the period we have been tracking them.
This does not mean every axe posted is of equal quality. Volume has grown as dealers have recognised the competitive importance of electronic axe distribution, and with higher quantity comes variation in quality. The question worth asking, though, is whether the axe ecosystem as a whole is functioning well enough to remain a useful signal. What we posit is that, with their occasional flaws, axes are still the most accurate predictor of the winning dealer in European markets across other available metrics today.
On axe size
There is an open question about whether small axes (sub-5MM in particular) should be treated differently, or whether minimum size thresholds would improve overall quality. It is a reasonable point to raise, and one we have looked into carefully.
What the data suggests today is that axed dealers outperform other dealers across every axe size bucket for aggressiveness of pricing and improvement during the trade. The performance differential is consistent and demonstrates care taken by axed dealers to provide better execution across axes of various sizes.
Median quote/CP+™ delta by axe size in EUR IG1
1Delta is calculated as the difference from CP+, our composite price that aims to predict where a trade will print – reflected here as 0. Negative values are interpreted as wider than CP+, values closer to 0 are more aggressive.

Median axe slippage by axe size in EUR IG2
2Positive slippage demonstrates improvement on advertised levels. Absence of values demonstrates levels that repeated the advertised level.

It is also worth noting that use cases for axes have broadened. Our largest clients automate 80% of their tickets—and for an automated order of 3MM, a 3MM axe from a dealer who reliably performs at that size is exactly the right signal to surface the dealers most likely to win. Where quality issues do exist, axe laddering with axe performance indicators would be a more precise tool for addressing size-related quality concerns.
At this time, however, across all inquiry sizes, clients appear to receive more aggressive levels from axed dealers than non-axed or anti-axed dealers.

Median quote/CP+ delta by inquiry size in EUR IG3
3Delta is calculated as the difference from CP+, our composite price that aims to predict where a trade will print – reflected here as 0. Negative values are interpreted as wider than CP+, values closer to 0 are more aggressive.

On two-way axes
Two-way axes attract understandable scepticism, as the dealer appears to have no meaningful directional conviction, but there are legitimate reasons for a dealer to be genuinely competitive on both sides: a large new-issue allocation where supply and demand are both active, or when a dealer operates an algo book and a trader book that run in parallel with different positioning. Trading outcomes with two-way dealers can, in these situations, be superior to the outcomes of trading with non-axed dealers.
Data shows that today, two-sided axe providers in EUR IG respond to 84% of inquiries, win 9.8% of these inquiries, and improve on their advertised levels by 1.8 cents. These outcomes are encouraging and allow us to believe that 2-sided axed dealers are overwhelmingly serious about trading on both sides.
That said, clients and dealers would benefit from more granular context clues for when two-sided axes are used. More precise taxonomy to accompany axes (e.g., distinguishing algo from trader axes, or inventory from non-inventory positions) would allow for buy-side clients to realise any advantages offered by two-way axes without removing legitimate liquidity signals.
What we are building
The most useful contribution platforms can make to this debate is to make quality indicators visible and to align incentives around it. That is what we are focused on.
Axe quality scoring is rolling out this year, giving clients transparent, data-driven visibility into their dealers’ performance on their axes. This directly addresses the structural incentive concern: if what determines selection is not whether a dealer is axed but how well they perform on axes, the incentive to post high-quality content is materially stronger.
Additionally, we want to ensure that clients are furnished with tools to surface the best dealers available for them in situations where axes are unavailable or ambiguous. AI Select, our AI-powered dealer selection engine, has been effective in predicting the best dealer in 59% of the backtested universe† by observing the dealer’s historical performance across 60 weighted trading metrics.
†This is the proportion of Smart Dealer Select inquiries where when top 3 AI Select-predicted dealers were invited, an AI Select dealer won the inquiry.

We have also invested in ensuring sufficient information flow to dealers. Dealers are informed of when automated dealer selection drove the order and when their axe attracted the order in. Better feedback to dealers on the inquiry should ensure that dealers can continue to service their axes well.
When source of the axe matters, algo vs. trader axe demarcation enables granular flagging that makes two-way axes more interpretable. Dealers can distinguish axes originating from algo books versus trader books, giving clients clearer context on the nature of the liquidity being offered.

A shared interest in getting this right
The conversations happening at FIX and across the industry on axe quality are valuable, and we want to be a constructive part of them. Our view is that the data, on balance, tells an overall encouraging story, but that there is real work to do on measurement, transparency, and incentive design to keep it that way.
We are committed to publishing the data that supports or nuances that view and to building the tooling that keeps the axe ecosystem honest. We welcome the nuanced discussion, and we look forward to the next iteration of this conversation.

We thank the FIX community for a thoughtful and constructive discussion.

title: Liquidity under pressure: What oil shocks really do to HY energy markets
text:
Liquidity under pressure: What oil shocks really do to HY energy markets
The return of oil toward $100 a barrel amid escalating tensions with Iran has triggered a familiar stress test for high-yield energy markets, where rising volatility is typically expected to erode liquidity.
But recent trading data tells a different story. Liquidity has not disappeared during this period of stress — it has become more electronified, and more valuable to access if you know where to look. On the MarketAxess platform, high-yield energy volumes have increased meaningfully even as broader market activity softened, while the price impact of each additional dealer response has risen sharply.
What the data actually shows
The shift begins with where trading is actually occurring. In the 4 months leading up to the conflict, high-yield energy activity on MarketAxess averaged roughly $75 million in average daily volume. In March, that figure rose to more than $100M. Over the same period, overall high-yield energy volume across TRACE declined. Pre-war, the HY energy market saw $5.6bn in average daily volume (ADV) across 13,100 trades on average. Post-war, that has adjusted to an ADV of $4.2bn across 10,800 HY energy trades according to TRACE data.
HY energy ADV MoM

Why liquidity fragmentation matters
At the same time, the economics of execution have changed materially. Prior to the onset of volatility, each additional response in HY energy delivered roughly two cents of price improvement. Since the conflict, that figure has increased to closer to three cents per additional response.
In practical terms, each incremental response is now more impactful — reflecting a market in which competition is more valuable as spreads widen and pricing becomes less certain.
Counting on liquidity
For HY energy traders, the message is clear: liquidity is still there, but it is less forgiving. As depth fragments and spreads widen, execution depends more on generating competition. The rise in response rates — from 6.4 to 7.4 per inquiry — translates into roughly 3 cents of improved execution, helping offset the cost of volatility. In oil-driven dislocations, liquidity is not just a market condition — it is a driver of performance.
Avg. HY energy responses per inquiry QoQ1
1 Note, before the conflict, each additional dealer response generated roughly ~2c of price improvement (TCA), and as mentioned, that figure post-war has increased to ~3c per additional response.

The bigger takeaway
Taken together, the data suggests a fundamental shift in how liquidity behaves under stress. Traditional indicators — lower overall volume, wider spreads — point to deterioration. But beneath the surface, liquidity is not vanishing. When volatility increases and liquidity decreases elsewhere, activity actually increases on our MKTX platform. In this environment, execution is no longer defined simply by access to liquidity. It is defined by the ability to generate competition.
For high-yield energy traders, that distinction matters. As dealer balance sheets tighten and risk becomes more selective, the dispersion between strong and weak execution outcomes increases. Trades that attract multiple responses continue to clear efficiently, while others face materially higher costs.
The result is a market where liquidity depth is no longer just a background condition — it is a direct driver of performance. In oil-driven dislocations, volatility does not eliminate liquidity. It raises the price of accessing it.

Open Trading: Sourcing liquidity in times of volatility
Recent geopolitical tensions are creating a new normal of volatility in the global credit markets. During these times of volatility, established trading patterns often break down. The usual playbook goes out the window, liquidity providers can step back, and market participants scramble to locate buyers and sellers.
When liquidity becomes fragmented, and price discovery grows more challenging, certainty of execution and reliable counterparties become more difficult. This is precisely where Open Trading® delivers value.
Open Trading is our global, all-to-all electronic marketplace that delivers smarter, faster, and more efficient trading. This means enabled participants can both take and provide liquidity regardless of jurisdiction or counterparty type. They can trade with specialist dealers, alternative liquidity providers, and real money clients at the touch of a button. Responses are co-mingled with the responses of their regular dealer panel as a client or fully anonymized as a dealer. Dealers taking liquidity now make up nearly one-third of Open Trading volumes, further demonstrating the diversity of liquidity available.
One of the key differentiators of Open Trading is the breadth of its network. In calmer markets, trading relationships tend to remain stable, and clients often concentrate flow among a smaller set of preferred dealers. They use Open Trading to further prove best execution. When volatility spikes and liquidity dries up, those relationships can often not be relied upon. Dependable price discovery becomes increasingly difficult, especially in emerging markets and high yield, where automation is less prevalent, pushing many traders back to voice.
During these periods of stress when traditional price discovery mechanisms struggle, Open Trading vastly expands the available liquidity pool, increasing the likelihood of finding a match. It improves trading outcomes and lowers transaction costs — both for providers and takers of liquidity. The result is more informed decision-making and improved confidence in execution.
Open Trading price improvement (MENA)†
†Difference between the winning OT price and the next best disclosed price.

Algorithmic trading adds stability
Another key evolution in recent years has been the growing use of algorithms from both established dealers and new alternative liquidity providers who turn to Open Trading to scale their risk recycling and provide unprecedented levels of liquidity as a result. Today, more algorithms are pricing bonds than ever before, and in larger sizes — often quoting up to $3–5 million in single inquiry size in liquid names and in many cases much more. 
These algorithms are becoming more active across all core sectors and increasingly remain switched on, even during volatile conditions. This consistency provides a stabilizing effect on prices and ensures that actionable liquidity remains visible on screen.
Historically, traders moved to voice during periods of uncertainty. But now with improved data, consistent algorithmic pricing, and the expanded reach of Open Trading, participants can confidently remain on the platform rather than reverting to phone-based execution.
This reliability is particularly valuable when sourcing liquidity in specialized names. For example, if a trader is seeking liquidity in a specific issuer, such as a regional energy company, the optimal counterparty may be limited. Open Trading’s all-to-all model increases the probability of locating domestic or onshore liquidity providers specific to that name, acting as an effective price finder when it is needed most.
A full suite designed for every trading scenario
Markets often shift toward more on-demand trading during volatility, especially voice and Request-for-Quote (RFQ) workflows. While some participants question inquiry quality in stressed environments, MarketAxess enhancements have helped improve engagement and response rates. For many clients and dealers, Open Trading has become the number one counterparty on the MarketAxess platform.
Remaining engaged with the full Open Trading network during times of market stress suits the majority of market participants, but not all. That’s why we offer a suite of protocols that lets the trader not only decide how to trade but who they trade with. We have new protocols that help bridge the gap between full disclosure and full anonymity.
Disclosed Open Trading is a hybrid functionality within Open Trading. It allows name give-up to counterparties within the Open Trading network, where participants do not have a direct relationship by settling through MarketAxess as the intermediary. This enables traders to receive the benefits of pre-trade name disclosure and relationship building. Full control of the inquiry distribution is possible as Disclosed Open Trading replicates full name give-up and can even be used to send to a single known dealer.
Disclosed Open Trading is just one way clients can utilize the Open Trading settlement facility on certain types of name-give-up trades. Crossing allows the externalization of internal fund transfers. Bridge Trading allows clients and dealers who do not have lines with each other to settle pre-agreed trades. 
Voice facilitation is often not associated with electronic trading. However, as a top-tier counterparty on the platform, we recognize that we need to provide a service worthy of a top-tier dealer, and that includes replicating many of the services a trading desk at a dealer would provide. The Open Trading desk’s staff includes ex-traders and brokers who can facilitate a variety of services, including block size work-ups and reflecting targets on expired inquiries, all in confidence, on voice.
Trading with confidence: reach, data, and consistency
No single execution method fits every scenario, and traders need access to a full spectrum of tools. Open Trading expands the liquidity pool and improves execution probability. Our data tools enhance price discovery when observable markets are thin. Algorithmic liquidity adds consistency and stability. RFQ workflows support targeted engagement.
Together, the MarketAxess trading suite empowers participants to navigate all market conditions with confidence — helping them find liquidity, achieve the best price, and execute with speed and efficiency.

text:
Precision without disruption: strengthening CHF trading workflows with integrated reference pricing
In the quality-focused world of private banking, execution is defined by control, consistency, and accountability. Priorities are placed on structured workflows, ensuring each trade is defensible and meets best execution obligations. Reference pricing plays a central role in that process, providing the benchmark against which execution quality is measured. 
For CHF bonds, the SIX Swiss Exchange has long served as this primary reference point, particularly for smaller orders and odd lots. It provides a familiar and trusted view of the market, supporting decisions that need to be transparent and aligned with recognised benchmarks. 
However, the process of checking exchange pricing has historically introduced inefficiency into otherwise streamlined workflows. Even as institutional liquidity continues to migrate to electronic request-for-quote protocols, traders have often needed to consult the SIX order book separately before execution. This creates a workflow break, requiring multiple systems and adding time to a process that depends on timeliness, precision and auditability.
The integration of SIX reference pricing into Axess IQ addresses this directly. By embedding live exchange levels alongside dealer axes, indications, and RFQ responses, the need to move between platforms is removed. Pricing validation and execution can now take place within a single environment, both pre-trade and during execution. 
This is not a change in how trades are approached. It is an operational refinement. Existing behaviours are preserved, but the process becomes more efficient, controlled and easier to evidence. For workflows that prioritise process integrity and efficiency, removing friction without introducing risk is critical.
Expanding the pricing framework beyond visible markets
While exchange pricing provides an important anchor, it does not always reflect the full depth of institutional trading conditions. Order books tend to capture smaller trade sizes and visible liquidity, whereas much of the real activity in CHF credit occurs outside that view. 
CP+™, the proprietary MarketAxess reference price, extends the pricing framework to reflect this broader reality. It is derived from trading activity across the MarketAxess network, including RFQ flows, streaming prices, and block trades from both local and global participants. This incorporates liquidity and pricing that does not appear on exchange venues. 
When combined with SIX pricing in Axess IQ, CP+ provides a complementary perspective. One reflects a recognised exchange benchmark, while the other captures where institutional investors are actively transacting across sizes and market conditions. The result is a more complete and statistically robust foundation for decision- making. 
For desks that rely on reference-driven execution, this additional layer of data enhances confidence. Limit setting becomes more informed, execution outcomes more predictable, and pricing decisions more clearly justifiable. This is particularly relevant in environments where avoiding adverse outcomes is just as important as maximising client alpha. 
Accessing institutional liquidity within a controlled workflow 
Liquidity access remains a defining factor in execution quality. MarketAxess aggregates a broad network of dealers and buy-side participants, creating a competitive environment for each inquiry. For CHF bonds, this results in tighter pricing and deeper liquidity than is typically available through exchange order books or bilateral trading channels. 
Crucially, this liquidity extends beyond what is visible. Dealer axes, risk-based pricing, and block appetite are all incorporated into the platform, representing interest that may not otherwise be accessible within traditional workflows. This provides a more accurate reflection of where trades can be executed at scale.
Within Axess IQ, this liquidity is fully integrated with pricing and reference data. The workflow remains data-driven, structured, and controlled, but access to institutional interest is materially expanded. This supports better execution outcomes while maintaining the process discipline that is required on the trading desk of a private bank. 
Supporting evolution across trade sizes
The immediate benefits of integrating SIX exchange pricing are most apparent in smaller and automated trades. Exchange order books have traditionally guided decision- making in these areas, particularly as a reference check. By embedding those levels directly into Axess IQ, automated workflows gain an additional safeguard. Orders can be executed electronically on MarketAxess with confidence that pricing remains aligned with established benchmarks. 
Over time, this integration is also likely to influence behaviour in larger block trades.
Historically, block-sized CHF trading has remained largely voice-driven, with exchange infrastructure used primarily for booking and reporting rather than liquidity discovery. However, as pricing confidence increases and workflows become more integrated, electronic RFQ protocols are well positioned to capture a greater share of this flow. 
In this context, the combination of SIX reference pricing, CP+, and aggregated institutional liquidity becomes particularly relevant. It supports a model where larger trades can be executed electronically without compromising on pricing transparency, control, or execution quality. 
A more precise execution standard 
Swiss private banking workflows are built on precision and consistency as basis for value generation for the client. Efficiency is valuable, but only when justified and controlled. Any enhancement must align with these priorities and integrate seamlessly into existing processes. 
By embedding SIX reference pricing into Axess IQ, MarketAxess strengthens the core elements of CHF trading workflows. Reference validation remains central, but is now integrated. Pricing insight is broadened through CP+, without replacing established benchmarks. Liquidity access is expanded, while best execution discipline is maintained. 
The result is a more precise execution environment—one that reduces operational friction, improves visibility, and supports better execution outcomes across all trade sizes.

text:
Sourcing liquidity through a connected ecosystem
Liquidity in fixed income markets spans multiple protocols, venues, and workflows, expanding across request-for-quote (RFQ), portfolio trading (PT), centralized order books, and peer-to-peer models. This fragmentation has created complexity for both buy-side and sell-side participants and a challenge in how to access the right liquidity at the right time. The most effective approach is a cohesive ecosystem that combines protocols, partnerships, and data.
At MarketAxess, we offer a variety of protocols that allow participants to seamlessly transition between execution styles, whether taking liquidity via RFQ, providing liquidity through Open Trading® (our global, all-to-all electronic marketplace) or leveraging PT workflows. Routing is intelligent between protocols and understands when to engage one dealer, a select group, or a broader network. Innovations such as our Opening & Closing Auctions protocol pools buy and sell orders across the platform to concentrate liquidity during the most critical times of the day, improving execution outcomes and transparency.
To further enhance connectivity across liquidity pools, we have prioritized integration with client workflows and strategic partnerships. For example, our partnership with DirectBooks connects primary issuance with secondary trading, enabling a more seamless transition from new deal indication to secondary market execution. It also addresses the disconnect between issuance and trading liquidity, which remains one of the key inefficiencies presented by the fragmentation in fixed income markets today.
In parallel, we are continuing to deepen integration with OMS/EMS platforms, allowing clients to maintain flexibility while accessing multiple liquidity pools. Traders can interact with diverse liquidity sources without unnecessary information leakage, all within existing workflows. This interoperability is critical in building a more seamless and scalable trading environment.
Across many client discussions about liquidity, one point is consistent: “It’s all about the data”—specifically, how data informs execution decisions such as dealer selection, protocol choice, and timing of trades.
We have invested heavily in proprietary datasets and analytics tools to improve liquidity discovery. AI-driven solutions, such as our pricing engine, CP+™, provide real-time insights into market depth and execution costs. CP+ sources proprietary trading information not only based on executed trades but also on the stack of inquiries and responses that did not trade, resulting in more accurate pricing and thereby enhancing pre-trade decision-making. Another data tool is AI Select, which helps clients optimize counterparty selection. Instead of “blasting” inquiries broadly, traders can engage a curated set of counterparties, improving response quality by only sending the inquiry to the counterparties most likely to respond.
The liquidity challenge in fixed income trading can be addressed through a combination of integrated connectivity across platforms and workflows, driven by real-time analytics and data-informed execution strategies, and strategic partnerships that bridge liquidity across markets. Together, our approach creates a seamless ecosystem for accessing the right liquidity at the right time.

Join me at FILS on June 16th at 10:05am as I dive into the intricacies of these liquidity challenges on the session titled, “Evaluating Strategic Partnerships: How Can You Ensure Consistent Liquidity Across Fragmented Markets.”

title: Targeted axes: precision, control and efficiency
text:
Targeted axes: precision, control and efficiency
For decades, sell-side traders have had a familiar problem: they have a specific axe, and they need to put it in front of the right clients fast, without broadcasting it to the market. The most reliable way to do that hasn’t changed in years: pick up the phone or fire off individual messages. But as soon as the list grows beyond a handful of names, the workflow slows down, context gets lost, and it becomes hard to scale with control.
Late last year, we launched Targeted Axes to take that manual, one-by-one outreach and turn it into a controlled, efficient, fully electronic workflow. Dealers can show a firm, disclosed list of axes (1 or many) to exactly the clients they choose, and buy-side traders can act on it immediately, while preserving the confidentiality and control that traders require.
From voice to electronification
Targeted Axes enables dealers to send firm, disclosed axes to a defined group of buy-side clients, whether that’s one counterparty or many, without widening the audience beyond what’s intended.
The workflow mirrors the familiarity of our Dealer RFQ workflow, where the sell-side trader enters the axe details, selects a distribution list, and sends. Distribution lists can be configured and reused, so the next time a similar instrument or trade type comes up, the trader reaches the same clients in seconds instead of rebuilding the outreach from scratch.
On the buy-side, the axe arrives on a dedicated screen with a pop-up notification, so it doesn’t get buried in a chat thread. In the same view, the trader immediately sees whether it lines up with existing interest through an opportunity count that shows how many resting RTS orders match that axe. That signal stays on the buy-side only, helping traders move quickly while preventing information leakage.
From there, engagement is fully electronic and firm. Buy-side traders can hit or lift automatically; link directly to RTS orders; counter on size or level; or “circle” an axe, placing it on hold while conducting due diligence. While circled, other traders are unable to automatically aggress the axe but they can still respond with their interest, and the dealer may elect to fill-or-kill the circle to execute away.
Circling removes one of voice trading’s most persistent sources of friction: uncertainty. However, it creates a new issue: the moment a buy-side trader circles an axe, its status updates in real time for everyone involved. All participants can see when an axe is circled, when it’s active, and when it’s no longer available. And because axes are firm, there’s no last look from the dealer, removing any ability to fade, reject or renegotiate.
An enhancement rolled out in our latest release for Swaps extends the workflow beyond single-line axes to fully disclosed, executable two-legged Swap and Switch package trades. Dealers can distribute firm Swap packages to selected client groups with defined firm limits on both legs and complete control over engagement. Buy-side traders receive actionable Swap axes directly in their Targeted Axes activity view, with package analytics: pick/give spread, price, G-spread, and maturity. Engagement happens at the package level only: clients can accept, counter, or circle, ensuring both legs execute simultaneously with full transparency for all participants.
One container, full transparency
All of this plays out in a single session window. Dealers post and manage multiple axes at once, watch responses come in, pull back unengaged axes, and respond to counters without losing the thread. Dealers gain focused buy-side attention with every step captured in a complete activity log.
For the buy-side, the experience stays equally focused. A dedicated activity tab surfaces axes that align with resting orders, making it easier to prioritize what matters and monitor multiple opportunities at once. Execution, counters, and order linking happen in real time, which reduces friction and speeds up decision-making. With Targeted Axes, buy-side traders can trust that what they’re seeing is actionable, relevant, and current.
What’s next?
The pilot phase of Targeted Axes has concluded with strong feedback from the traders who used it, confirming that the core workflows (targeted distribution, hit/lift, counters, and circling) hold up in the moments that matter most: when axes need to move quickly, cleanly, and with clear intent. 
The next chapter focuses on giving both sides even more control and flexibility. In the coming months, we’re rolling out expanded buy-side controls over what axes they want to see, along with additional engagement options—building on what the pilot taught us about how dealers and clients want to interact when liquidity is scarce, and timing is everything.
Stay tuned for further details on these enhancements. You can contact myself or your MarketAxess representative to learn more.

title: AxessPoint: Oracle—Investment-grade rating, high-yield reality
text:
AxessPoint: Oracle—Investment-grade rating, high-yield reality
Oracle (ORCL) was downgraded to BBB- by S&P in early July, from BBB to one notch above high-yield. Its 30-year bonds have widened 150 bps since September, when it raised $18bn of debt for AI infrastructure. ORCL now trades wide to many BB names after raising another $25bn in February. But does it truly trade like a high-yield bond? By many metrics compared to peers, ORCL 30-year bonds have gone from near-first to near-last, becoming more high-yield by the day:

- Its spreads are now wide of BB names: +25 bps to CHTR, +100 bps to VTRS, and +150 bps to many low BBB peers.

- The share of client RFQ trades won by an Open Trading® response is up from 20% to 30-40%, a share typically seen during periods of high volatility or in BB and single B bonds.

- It now moves 3 bps a day on average, in line with PARA and up from only 1 bp for much of 2025.

- Its more seasoned 30-year bond has a bid-ask of almost 3 bps, while its BBB peers are all under 1.5 bps.

Below we look at its three newest 30-year bonds: two issued as part of the hyper-scaling deals in February 2026 and September 2025, and one issued just before in February 2025. We compare them to many liquid 30-year benchmarks: high profile BB names like CHTR and PARA, tech BBB names that were (once) its peers like AVGO and INTC, and finally non-tech BBB names also in the news or highly liquid like BA, CVS, and HCA.

1. Spread
Except for PARA 4.95 ’50, ORCL trades wide to both BB 30-year bonds of comparable size. At +275, ORCL trades 25 bps wider than CHTR and 100 bps wider than VTRS, both liquid BB 30-years with over $1bn outstanding. As recently as summer 2025, ORCL at +125 traded tighter than almost all the bonds shown below.
*Data as of July 28th, 2026

2. Price change since Jan 1st 2025
The shift is particularly evident in ORCL’s price change. We compare ORCL to its peers for all 30-year senior bonds of at least $750mm deal size. Like an index, we start on Jan 1, 2025 and weigh each issuer’s daily price changes by amount outstanding. ORCL long bonds have deteriorated over 20% in price terms, worse than PARA and all its BBB peers.
*For illustrative purposes, clean price only – does not include coupons and accrued interest.

3. Open Trading share of trades
The share of client RFQ trades won by an Open Trading response typically rises with higher volatility and lower credit quality. For stressed credits and volatile markets, the value of the MarketAxess OT network rises to fill in liquidity gaps. ORCL's share by count doubled from 20% just before its first AI deal in September 2025, to 40% by the time of its second deal in February. An OT response wins a third of trades in ORCL currently, more in line with BB and even single B buckets, and above the 25% typically seen for investment grade.

4. CP+™ bid-ask spread
The bid-ask on ORCL's older pre-AI issue has converged with PARA 4.95 '50 to almost 3 bps. Its Sep '25 deal has a bid-ask comparable to CHTR 6.7 '55. Its most recent issue has a bid-ask of 2 bps, while more seasoned BBB peers all have a bid-ask near 1.5 bps and some as tight as 1 bp.

5. Average daily spread change
ORCL’s spreads to treasury now move 3 bps a day on average, in line with PARA 4.95 '50 and CHTR 6.7 '55 recently. Before its massive AI issuance, it used to trade +/- 1 bp per day, like most of its BBB peers still do.

Conclusion
While Oracle may still carry an investment-grade rating, its 30-year bonds are increasingly trading with high-yield characteristics. Wider spreads, steeper price deterioration, higher daily spread volatility and a rising Open Trading share all point to liquidity characteristics more commonly associated with BB credit than investment-grade peers. The market appears to be repricing Oracle’s AI-driven debt buildout in real time, with liquidity dynamics and trading behavior suggesting that investors are already treating Oracle as high-yield risk.

title: AxessPoint: Stellantis—sector pressure and issuer-specific repricing
text:
AxessPoint: Stellantis—sector pressure and issuer-specific repricing
On 10 February 2026, Moody’s downgraded Stellantis to Baa3 from Baa2, its lowest investment-grade rating, following substantial downward revisions to profitability and cash-flow expectations. Stellantis had also announced €22.2bn of charges associated with changes to its product roadmap, battery supply chain and warranty estimates. Volkswagen entered the period from a stronger rating position: S&P had affirmed its BBB+ rating in December 2025 but revised the outlook to negative amid pressure on profitability and free cash flow.
Unless otherwise stated, spreads, spread changes and bid-ask widths are expressed in basis points of yield spread. Open Trading® metrics are expressed as percentages, with changes reported in percentage points.

- Stellantis’ February reset and subsequent rating actions were followed by a materially larger spread repricing than among selected auto peers. The dislocation persisted across much of its senior curve, with parts trading wider than maturity-matched BB reference benchmarks. The liquidity indicators examined were comparatively resilient: bid-ask widths narrowed after an initial widening, while Open Trading participation remained comparatively high.

- By 9 March, credit spreads were wider than their pre-event medians across the selected auto groups. Volkswagen was 14.4bp wider, while Stellantis was 39.8bp wider.

- Comparing the pre- and post-event windows, median bond-level spread widening was 21.6bp for Stellantis, 5.8bp for Volkswagen and 5.0–7.7bp for the other selected auto peers. Stellantis’ spread premium to the selected auto-peer median increased by 15.9bp.

- Six of the 12 sampled Stellantis senior unsecured bonds traded wider than their respective maturity-matched BB reference benchmarks on at least 60% of observed pricing days.

Methodology: Pre-event window: 13 January–9 February 2026. Post-event window: 10 February–9 March 2026. Selected auto peers: BMW, Ford, General Motors, Mercedes-Benz, Renault, and Volkswagen. The pre-event window includes the 6 February business reset, so the comparison captures the broader reset-and-downgrade sequence rather than the 10 February downgrade in isolation.
Stellantis widened more sharply than selected auto peers
The February reset coincided with sector-wide widening, but the magnitude differed sharply. By 9 March, Stellantis’ CP+™ spread was 39.8bp above its pre-event median, compared with 14.4bp for Volkswagen and smaller moves across most selected peers. The divergence was therefore consistent with a pronounced issuer-specific component rather than a uniform auto-sector repricing.
Over the 60-trading-day period ending 4 September 2026, Stellantis bonds occupied the wider end of the selected auto peer range across most comparable maturities. The separation was particularly visible further along the curve, indicating that the repricing was not confined to a single bond or narrow maturity segment. Six of the 12 sampled senior unsecured bonds traded wider than their respective maturity-matched BB reference benchmarks on at least 60% of observed pricing days.
The relative dislocation persisted across much of the curve

Bid-ask widths partly normalised after the initial deterioration
For a fixed set of seasoned bonds, MarketAxess CP+ shows daily clean-price performance, indexed to 100 at the start of the period, and monthly median bid-ask width. Stellantis prices declined further than those of Volkswagen and the core-auto composite, although clean-price performance also reflects duration and rates exposure. Spread measures therefore remain the cleaner indicator of relative credit repricing.
Stellantis’ monthly median CP+ bid-ask width rose from 2.39bp in February to 3.20bp in April, before narrowing to 2.14bp in August. By August, it was close to Volkswagen’s 2.08bp, although it remained above the 1.76bp core-auto composite.

Open Trading diverged between seasoned senior bonds and new hybrids
Open Trading evidence was mixed. The rolling share for seasoned Stellantis senior bonds fell by 6.0 percentage points during the reset-and-downgrade window, from 19.1% to 13.1%; its median over the window was 17.3%. That median remained above the EUR BB, BBB, and A-or-better reference cohorts shown.
By contrast, the rolling Open Trading share increased by 11.2 percentage points between 9 April and 1 June across the three hybrids issued in March, pooled by completed RFQ count. Because these were new bonds, the increase should not be read as evidence of improving liquidity in the seasoned senior curve. Open Trading rose in newly issued hybrids, not in seasoned senior bonds.

Conclusion
Stellantis’ February credit reset marked more than a temporary sector-wide reaction. Its senior curve repriced materially against selected auto peers, with parts trading at spreads wider than their maturity-matched BB reference benchmarks. Yet the liquidity evidence was differentiated rather than uniformly weaker: bid-ask widths narrowed after the March–April increase, seasoned senior Open Trading participation remained above the reference cohorts shown, and the strongest later Open Trading increase was concentrated in newly issued hybrids. The evidence therefore points to a higher embedded credit premium without a comparable, sustained deterioration in the liquidity indicators examined here.

title: Brazil’s fixed income market turns electronic
text:
Brazil’s fixed income market turns electronic
For years, the Brazilian fixed income market operated on a paradox: it was one of the world’s most sophisticated sovereign debt markets but it still relied heavily on voice and manual trade execution. With new regulatory mandates and political uncertainty defining the market climate, that’s beginning to change.
A shift to electronic trading has been building since the Banco Central do Brasil and the National Treasury committed to a transparency-first agenda for local markets in 2019. Accelerating this trend is the more recent, early 2026 mandate primarily aimed at making the secondary market for Brazilian sovereign debt more liquid and observable. It specifically encourages the greater use of electronic trading. MarketAxess became one of four accredited platforms to support that initiative, to bring the same electronic workflow that transformed credit markets in New York and London directly into the Brazilian onshore ecosystem. The directive is working—BRL Títulos Públicos trading on MarketAxess is up 74% year-over-year through Q1 2026. 

The growth of electronic trading in Brazil

 +74%
 +51%
 +24%

 YoY Q1 2026
 YoY YTD through April 2026
 YoY onshore trading through April 2026

The regulatory effort is largely a reaction to a macroeconomic and geopolitical climate that has heightened the importance of liquidity and execution quality. Brazil’s quantitative easing cycle and a contested electoral calendar have combined with this backdrop to introduce greater pressure on market volatility, pricing stability and investor confidence. As spreads move more rapidly and volatility increases, transparent price-discovery becomes more critical, as does a clear audit trail. In that environment, electronic platforms offer defensibility and control in addition to efficiency. 
As a result, a broader behavioral shift among local market participants is growing. Onshore clients and dealers, who are historically slower to migrate away from traditional execution methods, are stepping up their adoption of electronic workflows alongside their global counterparts. Brazil onshore trading is up 24% through April, pointing to organic changes in trading behavior rather than activity driven solely by regulatory requirements. The adoption curve reflects a market that is becoming more structurally electronic by choice, not just by mandate. 
Brazil’s fixed income market is increasingly aligning with the electronic infrastructure and trading standards that have become established across the US and Europe over the past decade. As market participants navigate a more volatile and interconnected environment, transparency, competitive pricing and technological agility are becoming foundational requirements. Brazil’s transition toward a more electronic market structure is now less a question of direction than of pace.

title: CP+™ for ETFs: Improving ETF portfolio management with predictive pricing
text:
CP+™ for ETFs: Improving ETF portfolio management with predictive pricing
Kat Sweeney, Global Head of ETFs and Data Solutions at MarketAxess, sat down with Jeff Lenamon, Head of Portfolio Construction & Senior Portfolio Manager at DWS, to discuss how DWS has improved the performance of their ETFs by integrating CP+ into daily workflows and the create/redeem process. Starting his career in Fixed Income in 1998, Jeff is an industry veteran who has managed Credit ETFs since the 2000’s, including HYG and LQD during the financial crisis.
Kat Sweeney:
Much has been written about the growth and trading of Fixed Income ETFs, but there is little known about the complexities of actually managing an ETF. I joke, (but it’s true!) that you are one of the “OGs” of the ETF world—so can you set the scene for us?
Jeff Lenamon:
“Industry veteran” and “OG” makes me sound older than I am. But I was fortunate to be introduced to the asset class in the early stages.
Anyway, to your question: To create Fixed Income ETF shares, the ETF Portfolio Managers (PMs) work with Authorized Participants (APs) who provide liquidity in ETF shares to clients. Since most portfolios hold upwards of thousands of bonds, the PMs negotiate optimized creation units called Custom In-Kind Baskets (CIBs) to facilitate the process. This negotiation is an active process between the ETF PM and the AP. While trading of an ETF happens throughout the day at varying prices, a creation is priced at the Net Asset Value (NAV) which is determined by valuing the portfolio at an End of Day Evaluated Price. 
While the CIB creation process offers many benefits, there are specific challenges an ETF PM faces, largely due to how the fund synthetically buys or sells underlying securities at the Evaluated Price. PMs must evaluate the impact that each CIB will have on the fund, to ensure he or she is not introducing tracking error.
“How a fund is marked, isn’t just an internal priority—it’s a competitive necessity.”

Kat:
Let’s dig into that a little more. We know that fund managers try to minimize tracking vs. the benchmark, focusing on the “market factor.” What other factors can influence the performance of the fund?

Jeff:
Yes, that’s right. As you say, fund managers have traditionally focused on trying to minimize tracking vs. their benchmark across issuer, sector, ratings, maturity, and capital structure. However, pricing skew can also play a contributing factor into tracking error and ultimate fund performance.
As you know, unlike Equity ETFs, where the NAV is determined by the official closing price of each stock, Fixed Income ETF NAVs are determined by “Evaluated Prices” that are offered by multiple vendors. The complexities of our market and the illiquidity of some bonds can lead to distortions—pricing skew—between the Evaluated Price and where the market is actually trading. Fund managers will routinely “challenge” Evaluated Prices they believe are off market, but this process typically happens only after the prices are published, meaning they don’t pick up the skew intra-day.
When I moved into the PM role, we focused on the difficult and complex task of managing the CIB process and monthly rebalances. We realized that the traditional approach to evaluating pricing skew could be addressed effectively by leveraging some of the liquidity and pricing products we used in my prior trading role. This was important—because having confidence in the end-of-day price and being able to adequately gauge bid-ask spread and liquidity estimates of bonds, is fundamental to the successful management of our funds.

Kat:
…and so enters MarketAxess CP+…

Jeff:
Yes. We introduced CP+ predictive pricing across our portfolio management, optimization, and trading processes, developing a streamlined “skew assessment” that assesses the discrepancies between the funds’ expected end-of-day prices vs. CP+ throughout the day.
This approach helps the team identify outlier bonds, reducing the potential to deliver a “cheap” bond via a creation or a “rich” bond via a redemption. At the fund level, we can use CP+ to determine intraday moves and realistic market execution levels, which provides greater transparency into skew estimates, so our talented PM team potentially reduces tracking errors and ensures NAVs are being marked efficiently.
“CP+ provides our funds with a more accurate representation of realistic market execution levels. CP+ is a great tool to help us potentially minimize tracking error and optimize fund performance, which is a great outcome for our clients and could give us a competitive advantage.”

Kat:
It’s the perfect example of how the ETF ecosystem is driving innovation in both market mechanics and the data solutions that support them. Innovation that wouldn’t happen without the support and collaboration between you, DWS and MarketAxess, so I do want to say a big thank you to you and your team for your partnership.
If you don’t mind, I will conclude briefly:
“The bottom line is that ETFs are influencing market structure, and fund managers need to adapt accordingly, integrating new data solutions and technologies into their portfolio construction and management workflows.”

This includes, but is not limited to, better and more accurate evaluated pricing models; real-time predictive pricing; and access to deeper and broader credit liquidity pools. Those who do it successfully, as Jeff has described, will see immediate competitive value for their funds, and will be able to measure, automate and execute against their desired portfolio strategies with confidence.

About CP+ and our Evaluated Pricing partnership with S&P Global:
CP+ is the MarketAxess award-winning, algorithmic pricing engine which provides nowcast prices, calibrated to reflect trades as closely as possible without introducing bias.
Last year, MarketAxess and S&P Global announced a historic pricing partnership where CP+ is ingested into their Evaluated Bond Price (EVB). This partnership bridges the gap between CP+'s predictive price, used for intraday trading decisions, and the Evaluated Price, used to value FI ETF NAVs. To find out more, click here.
MarketAxess would like to thank Jeff Lenamon and the entire DWS team for their continued support and consultation, so that we can continue to provide best-in-class data solutions for our clients.
