title: AxessPoint: Axe quality and reliability evolution across major markets
text:
AxessPoint: Axe quality and reliability evolution across major markets
Highlights

- Axe quality is improving in line with growing contribution. We see increasing dealer participation & bond coverage across major markets – alongside tighter pricing and more reliable liquidity provision.

- Axed trading significantly outperforms non-Axed activity across response rates, win rates, and execution quality when using CP+™ pricing data to assess quality and performance.

Axes matter to buy-side clients because they provide a clear, actionable signal of dealer interest. By highlighting where liquidity sits, axes help traders select the most responsive dealers, and improve execution outcomes - particularly when liquidity is fragmented or when market impact is a concern. Clients use axes to identify which dealers are best positioned on a given bond, to streamline dealer selection through tools like our own Smart Select, and to engage more confidently in high-touch or block-size trades.
Growth in axe content
Axe contributions expanded substantially in Q4 2025 across both US and European investment-grade markets. US HG averaged 8,291 bonds per day from 30 dealers, representing a 21% increase from Q2 2025. EUR IG reached 7,046 bonds daily from 51 dealers, marking an even stronger 25% growth over the same period.
The higher dealer count in EUR IG combined with the steeper growth trajectory indicates particularly strong adoption of axe-based workflows in European markets. This expansion reflects growing dealer commitment to disclosed liquidity provision and signals that axe content is becoming essential for competitive positioning.
Improving quality of pre-trade content
Beyond contribution, the reliability of axe content improved meaningfully throughout 2025. Dealers' axe levels have become more precise, with a greater proportion of responses showing minimal or no slippage.

EUR IG Quarterly axed response quality (2025)

US HG quarterly axed response quality (2025)

EUR IG responses showed zero slippage 65% of the time by Q4, up from 57% in Q2. US HG demonstrated similarly sharper improvement, with no-slippage responses rising from 44% to 48%, and responses within half the CP+ Bid/Offer Spread of their Axe or better jumping from 62% to 69%. This reflects dealers' growing sophistication in axe management and increased confidence in committing to tighter disclosed levels.

EUR IG vs US HG axed response quality by axe size bucket Q4 2025

Splitting Axed responses by the size of the Axe, we do not see a correlation between increasing axe size and degrading Axe quality. In EUR IG, ‘1MM-5MM’ Axes saw the best response quality, followed by the ‘>=5MM’ bucket. US HG dealers saw the best response levels vs their Axes for the ‘100K-1MM’ bucket, followed by ‘>=5MM’. Neither product saw responses with greatest slippage in the block Axe sizes.
Axe performance vs wider platform activity
Q4 data reveals that axed content drives materially superior trading outcomes across all markets for sizes >=1MM. Response rates are 2-5x higher when dealers are axed, and win rates are 1.5-2.7x greater.

Q4 2025 Cross-Market Performance (1MM+)

Axed dealers show dramatically higher engagement: 2.1x higher response rates in EUR IG, 2.9x in US HG, and 5.3x in US EM - indicating strong reliability and liquidity interest from Axes. When Axed, dealers also win tickets at significantly higher rates, with Axed dealers’ win rates (*) in EUR IG at 2.7x that of non-Axed dealers, and 1.5-1.7x for US HG and EM.
Relative to penetration of Axes, EUR IG demonstrates the most mature Axe ecosystem on MarketAxess, with 61% of inquiries inviting at least one Axed dealer, and 48% of inquiries being won by an Axed dealer. US HG (26%) and US EM (15%) show lower but growing adoption, suggesting significant expansion potential in US markets.
*Win Rate: % of dealer responses that won on inquires.

Conclusion
In Q4 2025, axe-based trading demonstrated substantial growth and improved quality across major bond markets, significantly outperforming non-axed activity in response rates, win rates, and execution quality. By using CP+ pricing data, we can definitively measure the quality and performance of Axes vs non-Axed trades and see the improvement in reliability of axe content during 2025 as dealers became more precise in their axe levels and commit to tighter disclosed levels.

title: AxessPoint: Credit markets showed resilience through April volatility
text:
AxessPoint: Credit markets showed resilience through April volatility
Highlights:

- The credit market demonstrated resilience amid April volatility, maintaining robust trading volumes across various sectors.

- Credit spreads widened due to flight-to-quality flows, while bid-ask spreads remained contained compared to previous periods of extreme stress. In contrast to the COVID-19 crisis, dealers stayed active and algos continued to provide liquidity, underscoring the successful growth of algo usage across liquidity providers.

- PT volume rose with overall market activity, maintaining a stable share and continuing as a reliable tool for credit markets.

- The impact was uneven globally—US markets saw the sharpest disruption but the fastest recovery, while EU and EM markets remained more stable overall.

During the April 2025 tariff-driven market turbulence, credit markets experienced notable but relatively orderly volatility, in contrast to the severe dislocation seen during the COVID-19 liquidity crisis. The April 2nd tariff announcement in the late afternoon resulted in policy uncertainty, causing notable market fluctuations during the following week. Sentiment stabilized following a U.S.-announced 90-day pause on additional tariffs (excluding China) on April 9th (early afternoon).
Bid-ask spreads widened substantially during this period, though far less than in 2020. During April turbulence, average bid-ask spreads for US HG reached 9.11bps, reflecting a brief reduced market liquidity period—though still significantly tighter than the 44.62bps recorded during the peak of COVID-19 market stress. Importantly, bid-ask spreads normalized swiftly without the need for large-scale monetary intervention, highlighting improved market functioning and a more tempered assessment of the economic impact of the tariff shock. At the same time, trading activity picked up significantly, with TRACE-reported volumes in US HG reaching record highs. The peak occurred on April 8th, with a total of $55.9 billion traded that day.

US HG Bid-ask spread: April volatility vs COVID-19 period

US HG TRACE volume: April volatility vs COVID-19 period

Market depth declined, though the scale of the reduction was modest relative to the COVID-19 episode, and liquidity recovered quickly. In US HG, the average number of prices per RFQ dropped from 13.2 to 6.6 on April 9 but quickly rebounded to 11.3 within a week. By contrast, during the COVID-19 shock, dealer responsiveness remained depressed for a prolonged period. Algo liquidity fell more sharply than non-algo liquidity in 2020 as evidenced by a 10-percentage-point drop in the share of prices back coming from algos—from 60% to 50%. During the recent volatility period, algos showed greater resilience in April with their contribution to overall liquidity provisioned consistently around 80%. This stability underscores the strengthened role of algos in supporting market function during volatility. Similarly, as noted in our recent AxessPoint on algos in block trading, the share of algo responses in block trades has grown significantly over the past four years, highlighting its rising importance in both U.S. and EUR credit markets.

US HG average number of responses: April volatility vs COVID-19 period

US HG % Prices coming from algos: April volatility vs COVID-19 period

PT activity remained stable during the April volatility, with volumes rising in line with broader market activity. PT continues to offer an efficient channel for executing large risk transfers, even though the execution costs for PT client sells began to rise as market volatility picked up. The absolute volume of PT increased alongside broader market flows, and its share of total activity remained steady during the event—highlighting PT’s established and consistent role in the credit market.

US HG PT volume/share (TRACE)

From a regional perspective, the US market reacted the most sharply but also recovered the fastest. Bid-ask spreads for US HG widened by as much as 231% in price but returned to normalcy quickly after April 9. In contrast, bid-ask spreads for EUR IG and USD EM widened more modestly —by 67% and 49% respectively —but remained elevated for a longer period. The divergence was also evident in trading volumes. EUR IG TraX® volumes rose by only 17.5%, whereas US HG volumes surged 59.5% relative to the 2024 average, underscoring the more dynamic response of the US market.

Bid-Ask spread: April volatility across markets

Conclusion
The April volatility highlighted the growing resilience of credit markets compared to past shocks like COVID-19, reinforcing investor confidence in engaging with the market. The increased use of dealer algos and the steady performance of PT underscore how automation and new protocols are strengthening market structure. As these tools become further integrated into trading workflows, they will be key to navigating volatility and enhancing execution efficiency.

Appendix: Comparative metrics highlight resilience across markets
Bid-ask spreads remained contained, and spread dispersion rose only modestly, signaling a more resilient market alongside solid trading volumes globally.
Open Trading® played a key role in supporting liquidity, driving more than doubled the price improvement for US HG and delivering meaningful improvements across other markets.

AxessPoint: Diverse participants create liquidity opportunities during credit market stress
By David Krein and John Keller | 8 April 2020
Print

Text

*Editor's note [April 7, 2025]: The strategies outlined in this 2020 article continue to prove valuable in today's market environment. Our analysis remains a timely resource for traders seeking to optimize execution quality during periods of heightened volatility.

In today's turbulent markets, we're witnessing volatility reminiscent of the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic. Last week's data revealed Open Trading® penetration in US High Grade bonds reaching 39%, delivering price improvements of 1.87 bps. US High Yield exhibited a similar pattern with 38% penetration and price improvements of 37 cents. For strategic insights on navigating these challenging conditions, we invite you to revisit our 2020 AxessPoint on unlocking liquidity during market volatility.*

Highlights

- Bond ETFs traded at a premium or discount to their “fair” value, measured by the bid/offer levels of their underlying bonds, throughout recent credit market volatility.

- On April 9th, when the Federal Reserve expanded their QE program to include High Yield bonds, ETF share prices traded at a premium to their underlying holdings.

- The Open Trading marketplace allowed participants to connect and take advantage of this arbitrage opportunity.

Arbitrage opportunities
Under typical market conditions, corporate bond ETF share prices lie in or around the fair value of their underlying bonds, calculated using CP+™ bid/offers. However, under recent extreme conditions, ETF share prices have moved outside the NAVs, i.e. fair value, of their underlying securities.
US IG corporate bond ETF, LQD, share price ($) vs CP+ NAV on April 9th
US HY corporate bond ETF, HYG, share price ($) vs CP+ NAV on April 9th
 
The most pronounced example of this was on April 9th, when the Federal Reserve announced an additional $2.3 trillion to its QE program, including High Yield bonds and Junk ETFs. A global market rally ensued where arbitrage opportunities emerged in Bond ETFs. The US IG corporate bond index, LQD, traded at a $1.45-$3.62 premium to the NAV of the underlying bonds, while the US HY corporate bond index, HYG, traded at a $2.3-$6.55 premium throughout the day.
More recently, on April 21st, corporate bond ETFs were trading at a discount to their fair value as oil turned negative for the first time in its history, leading to a global market sell-off. The US IG and HY ETFs, LQD and HYG, traded at discounts of as much as 60 cents and 109 cents, respectively, versus the “fair” value measured by CP+ bid/offer levels.
Connecting participants to engage liquidity
Arbitrage opportunities remain within ETF markets as volatility persists and underlying credit market spreads remain elevated. During recent volatility, we observed that ETF participants, as well asset managers and other non-bank institutions, were an active part of the liquidity transfer mechanism [see: “AxessPoint: Diverse participants create liquidity opportunities during credit market stress”]. The diverse trading connections facilitated by Open Trading allowed participants to take advantage of this arbitrage opportunity and maximize their liquidity options.
 
Redefining real-time bond ETF pricing
CP+ (fka Composite+) is MarketAxess’ proprietary AI-powered pricing engine for corporate bonds. It produces an unbiased, two-sided market for more than 25,000 instruments globally. title: AxessPoint: Portfolio Trading and price discovery in US IG and HY markets
text:
AxessPoint: Portfolio Trading and price discovery in US IG and HY markets
Executive Summary:

- Portfolio trading (PT) enhances liquidity in difficult-to-trade bonds with its basket-based "all-or-nothing" method. It has gained popularity among traders, increasing volumes and market share for IG and HY trading recently.

- PT is particularly beneficial for less liquid US Investment Grade and High Yield bonds. Some bonds trade primarily within PTs, helping to make more of the market tradable and, as such, aiding price discovery.

- Although PT pricing is done at the basket level, reducing focus on line-item accuracy, the gap between PT and RFQ pricing precision is narrowing.

In our recently published Portfolio Trading vs RFQ List White Paper, we discussed how Portfolio Trading offers benefits for traders looking to trade illiquid bonds. One of the advantages of the PT protocol is that when included in a well-balanced basket, line items with lower liquidity scores typically receive more favorable outcomes compared to execution with RFQ lists.
To expand on this concept, we dive deeper into PT as a mechanism for price discovery for US IG and HY bonds. As illustrated in the white paper, the generally held tenet is that portfolio trading is preferred for illiquid bonds. This is at least partially attributed to traders taking advantage of the protocol to attend to bonds that they may have little to no chance to trade otherwise. We can confirm this by observing several low-liquidity bonds traded primarily through PT.
Additionally, we also evaluated the pricing precision of PT and RFQ execution against CP+™, MarketAxess’ proprietary real-time AI pricing engine. From this, we can measure the precision of price discovery from PT as the market adopts this new protocol.
Rise in PT volume
For the last three years, PT has seen explosive growth in absolute volume and share of TRACE volumes. IG volumes rose from $122 billion in Q3 2023 to $275 billion by Q1 2025 , jumping from 7.4% to 10.4% of TRACE volumes. HY PT saw similar growth, rising from $32 billion to $74 billion, jumping from 6.2% to 10% of TRACE volumes.

Volume in Portfolio Trading in US IG

Volume in Portfolio Trading in US HY

Portfolio Trading accounts for a higher percentage of all trade activity for Illiquid bonds
As mentioned in our PT vs RFQ white paper, liquidity plays a major role in the composition of a PT basket. In the most efficient portfolio trades from a cost perspective, traders use PT to blend a mix of illiquid bonds in the same basket as liquid bonds. We measure liquidity for this case using the MarketAxess Relative Liquidity Score (RLS), which measures bonds on a scale from 1 (least liquid) to 10 (most liquid). More information on the score methodology can be found here.

Share of TRACE trades via PT by Liquidity Score - HG
From the above chart, we see that between Oct 2024 and March 2025 in IG, for bonds with at least one trade, on a per bond basis an average of 18.04% of trading activity is executed through PT for bonds with low liquidity score (<5), whereas for bonds with high liquidity score (≥8), only 10.18% of trading activity are executed through PT. This shows a clear divide between the importance of PT between the liquid and illiquid end of the market.

Share of TRACE trades via PT by Liquidity Score - HY

We can do a similar analysis for HY. From the chart below, we see that for the same period, on a per bond basis an average of 21.74% and 25.30% of trading activity is executed through PT for bonds with low and middle liquidity score respectively, whereas for bonds with high liquidity score, only 13.87% of trading activity are executed through PT.

CP+ Median Absolute Deviation for Portfolio Trade and RFQ
CP+ is designed to predict trade prices for institutional size trades (≥150k). It uses a consistent methodology across various market conditions, making it a reliable benchmark for measuring pricing precision. In the charts below, we plot the median absolute deviation (MAD) of MarketAxess platform traded levels to CP+ to measure the pricing precision of PT and RFQ.

Median Absolute Deviation by PT flag in HG - On Platform
While PT MAD used to be consistently higher than RFQ MAD, reflecting lesser line-item level pricing precision for PTs compared to all other trades to RFQ, we see this difference diminishing significantly in recent quarters. This indicates that the price discovery effect of PT is close to that of RFQ, as PT pricing accuracy at the basket level is increasingly like RFQ.

Median Absolute Deviation by PT flag in HY - On Platform

In HY, PT pricing quality was initially lower than RFQ in 2023, with median absolute deviation to CP+ at $0.17 for PT and $0.13 for RFQ. However, by Q1 2025, PT pricing deviation reduced to $0.10, close to the RFQ deviation of $0.09, indicating similar pricing precision as PT's share of trades increased.
Conclusion
Portfolio Trading has surged significantly in both volume and its share of TRACE activity over recent years. This evolution underscores the vital role Portfolio Trading plays in price discovery, particularly for illiquid bonds, which see a higher percentage of their activity within PT baskets. Remarkably, even though PT pricing is negotiated at the basket level, its pricing precision at the line-item level has increasingly mirrored traditional trading protocols like RFQ, enhancing overall market efficiency and price discovery.

title: AxessPoint: The expanding role of algos in block trading and market liquidity
text:
AxessPoint: The expanding role of algos in block trading and market liquidity
Highlights

- Algos currently supply liquidity to 96% of US HG, US HY, EUR IG and EUR HY client RFQs on the MarketAxess platform and are rapidly expanding into block trades (≥5MM).

- Inquiries in US HG saw the share of responses coming from algos jump from 12% to 37% for 5-10MM sizes and from 1% to over 16% for ≥10MM orders in the past four years.

- Unique bond coverage by algos has grown by 82% since Q1 2021, ensuring near-complete coverage of key ETFs like LQD and HYG.

- In the 5–10MM range for EUR IG, the share of inquiries with one or more algo responses surged from 45% to 70% in just two years, demonstrating a shift toward expanding algo liquidity across markets.

- The evolution of algorithmic trading is reshaping the future of electronic fixed income trading by enhancing liquidity sourcing and execution outcomes across market segments.

Dealer algorithms are liquidity provisioning programs that quote prices back to RFQs using fully automated systems. They now command a significant and growing share of trading volume in the largest market segments, while rapidly expanding into the HY space (both US and EUR). This rise has been fueled in part by the growth of the electronic bond market and by the increasing availability and depth of data from platforms, allowing dealers to continuously refine pricing and liquidity‐prediction models. In Q1 2025, US HG algos were on average providing 11 responses per inquiry and were the counterparty on 88% of trades, which is up 21 percentage points from Q1 2021. It is becoming clear that algos are dominating the liquidity pool and will continue to increase in importance.
In particular, the role of algos in executing large-volume transactions is quite significant. This trend is especially evident in block trades where algo-driven trades continue to grow steadily each quarter. The increasing reliance on algorithms not only boosts efficiency and speed but also enhances market depth. The continued expansion of algorithmic trading in the bond market is expected to further transform traditional trading structures and practices, driving changes in how liquidity is sourced.

Percent of responses from algos by quarter & size bucket US HG

Looking at US HG activity on the MarketAxess platform we can see that from Q1 2021 to Q1 2025, the percent of responses coming from algos for inquiries of size 5-10MM has increased from 12% to 37%. For inquiries of size ≥10MM, algorithmic responses have surged from 1% to over 16% in four years. This same trend is also very prominent when we examine the percentage of inquiries with more than one response coming from algos. For inquiries of size ≥10MM, the percentage has seen a massive increase from 10% to 78% in the past four years.

Percent of responses from algos by quarter & size bucket US HY

Focusing on the US HY market, we see a remarkable shift in algorithmic participation over recent years. In Q1 2021, only 20% of responses to inquiries ranging from 1-2MM in size were generated by algos. In Q1 2025 we are observing even greater levels of algorithmic penetration in trades of 3MM and above. In 2021, these larger inquiries had only 7% of responses originating from algos, but in Q1 2025, it had grown to 21%.
This increasing share of algo activity is seen across all markets in the 5-10MM range — US HG currently has 93% of inquiries with more than one algo response, US HY at 64%, EUR IG at 70%, and EUR HY at 29%.

Percent of Inquiries with ≥1 Algo Response for 5-10MM

Provider algorithms also have wide coverage in terms of unique bonds and size of orders. In Q1 2025, roughly 11,700 unique US HG bonds were covered by algos which represents a 32% growth from the 8,900 bonds covered in Q1 2021. As the universe of available bonds increases, algos are moving in tandem to maintain their growing coverage. This liquidity results in coverage for 99.8% of CUSIPs in the LQD ETF and 95.8% of CUSIPs inquired for on MarketAxess. For US HY, roughly 3,100 unique bonds are covered representing 95.8% of CUSIPs in the HYG ETF.

CUSIPs covered by algos

And it is not a handful of algos that are providing this coverage—from MarketAxess platform activity we can see that 8.7K out of the 11.7K US HG bonds are covered by 10 or more algos while only 2K bonds are covered by 5 or less. A slightly different dynamic emerges in US HY algo coverage since 900 out of the 3.1K unique bonds are covered by 10 or more algos while 1.8K are covered by 5 or less. Traders can feel much more confident that they will have competitive and fast pricing on their RFQs due to the growing presence of algos.
Additionally, the universe covered by algos has been steadily expanding across both size and liquidity profile. The tables below show how responses from algos vary across liquidity and quantity dimensions. The Liquidity Buckets represent groupings of our Relative Liquidity Score. Over the past four years, US HG has seen the percentage of responses coming from algos roughly double in larger-size segments. For example, in the 2MM-3MM bucket, algo responses have jumped from averages in the mid-20s in Q1 2021 to over 60–71% in Q1 2025. More extreme trends are observed in the 3MM-4MM and 4MM-5MM buckets, where increases of over 300% indicate that even as trade sizes grow, algos are now able to provide robust liquidity and pricing.

Percent of responses from algos US HG Q1
In US HY, the growth is even more dramatic with several segments more than tripling their algo participation. In the 5-7 liquidity 2MM-3MM segment, the percentage of responses from algos has grown from approximately 12% in Q1 2021 to 33% in Q1 2025. Additionally, for inquiries >3MM, the percentage of responses from algos have increased from roughly 4% to 20%, underscoring that high-volume, HY trades are now supported by a significantly enhanced liquidity pool.

Percent of responses from algos US HY Q1

These responses are also leading to increased trades with algos as the counterparty. Between Q1 2021 and Q1 2025, the share of trades with algos as the counterparty for orders over 1M in US HG increased by roughly 30 percentage points. In US HY, the proportion of algo trades for trades over 1M grew by about 20 percentage points.
Similar trends are seen in the European market across EUR IG and EUR HY with increases in both the percentage of responses and trades coming from algos.
The tables below show various metrics segmented by trade size for US HG and US HY. The US HG data shows that for larger trade sizes (5–10MM and >10MM), the MarketAxess platform delivers robust liquidity with competitive pricing. For instance, on the >10MM bucket – which represents 8.2% of inquiry volume – there is an average of 8.4 responses and a hit rate of 85.4%, indicating efficient execution and minimal price impact.

US HG Q1 2025 metrics
*RLS = Relative Liquidity Score
Similarly, there is evidence to support executing larger block trades in high-yield markets. The >3MM bucket averages 5.3 responses with a hit rate of 68.8%, reinforcing that block-sized trades can secure competitive pricing and reliable liquidity.

US HY Q1 2025 metrics

The growth of algorithmic trading has had a transformative effect on the bond market, significantly enhancing market liquidity and pricing efficiency. Better RFQ and trade data, along with improved models, have enhanced algo pricing capabilities, encouraging dealers to take on more risk. As the share of algo responses continues to rise across market segments and trade sizes, traders are becoming confident in executing larger orders electronically.
The rapid expansion of algo participation—particularly in larger size transactions—has not only improved execution quality but also fostered greater competition and speed in pricing. The increased coverage of unique bonds and the continued evolution of algorithmic strategies have created a large liquidity pool, empowering traders to engage in higher-value trades with greater confidence. This trend is expected to persist, with algorithmic trading playing an increasingly dominant role in shaping the future of fixed income market dynamics.

title: AxessPoint: Tradability deep dive—insights powered by an enhanced liquidity metric
text:
AxessPoint: Tradability deep dive—insights powered by an enhanced liquidity metric
Tradability is our machine learning based AI model that is calibrated to predict market depth on a bond, side, and size level. Tradability is primarily used for estimating responsiveness for a potential RFQ, but there are several supplemental insights that can be extrapolated with the knowledge of provider interest and market direction.

- What to trade: Tradability assesses the current, absolute liquidity of an individual bond—helping traders determine whether a specific security can be executed efficiently right now, based on live market conditions.

- How to trade: The difference between Tradability buy and sell values (skew) can be used as an indicator of pre-trade costs as well as future potential to unwind an order.

- When to trade: Intra-day updates of the Tradability model give insight into current conditions and the market’s reaction to news on both a bond/ticker level as well as a market-wide basis.

Tradability is a tool that can be used as a standalone data input or as an expansion of our existing RLS (Relative Liquidity Score) product. RLS provides a defined measurement of the current liquidity for an individual bond, highlighting the potential ease that a trader can expect to transact in that instrument. Bonds with a higher RLS see more responses, smaller bid-ask spreads, and improved transaction costs (TCA). Tradability has a similar linear relationship for trades on bond/side/size situations with higher predictions.
We see a strong linear correlation between the number of responses an RFQ gets and expected execution quality. Additionally, Tradability goes further than RLS by not only being bond specific in its prediction but giving a score that is relevant for a particular order, due to the fact that it considers order side, size, and time of day. This directly leads to a further use case of the Tradability data set — it can be used to show not only which bonds to trade, but also how and when to trade. While traditional RLS can be used as a point of comparison between bonds to see which is more fit, Tradability can help us map out entry and exit liquidity due to its size and side characteristics.
An important value that we can derive from Tradability data is skew, which measures the difference between the buy and sell predictions on a bond and size. The higher the skew value is, the cheaper it will be to purchase a bond, with differences measuring at 7-10 cents depending on prevailing market sentiment (figure 1). However, selling off that particular holding later may be costly if market direction holds. One potential outlet for orders like this may be through portfolio trading. As has been discussed in previous pieces like our PT vs RFQ white paper, illiquid line items in portfolio orders tend to see favorable execution outcomes when included in a well-balanced basket. This opens the opportunity to potentially acquire a bond with high skew cheaply via RFQ and exit the position later via PT.

Figure 1: RFQ TCA by Skew/Side
An example of Tradability aiding in how to trade can be seen in Auto-X™ RFQ. Historically, RLS has been used as a pre-trade selection criterion for automation eligibility. Tradability goes one step further by being not only instrument but also side and size specific. In this situation, Tradability can be used as a reliable guidepost for order selection. As can be seen in the chart below (figure 2), even for high liquidity bonds (defined as RLS of 7 and above) there are over 400 ISINs per day that have a Tradability skew of 3 or greater in either direction.
At times we observe cases at the bond or market level where the skew inverts, with sell interest outpacing buys. In a recent example here, we can see that due to issuer/bond level liquidity differences even bonds that would look identical from a liquidity score perspective see vastly different Tradability outcomes, either skewed towards buys, sells (inverted), or flat (figure 3).
Figure 2: Average daily number of ISINs by Skew

Figure 3: Tradability Skew for similar bonds (RLS 10, 5-year maturity bucket, Oil-Gas-Exploration, 100k-1MM)
Intra-day updates of Tradability can also give an indicator of market reaction to news and liquidity events. A recent notable example of this was the April 2025 volatility spike seen across the market. As uncertainty rose, we observed a sharp difference in market-wide Tradability predictions. Between President Trump’s announcement on April 2nd and the peak of market volatility from April 8-10th, Tradability predictions dropped roughly 20% on a market-wide basis, reflecting uncertainties felt by liquidity providers (figure 4). More granularly, there were several occasions where average Tradability predictions fell by nearly an entire response on an hour-over-hour basis intraday*. 

Figure 4: Median Tradability values vs April 1st, 2025

In conclusion, Tradability is a tool that has a wide set of use cases across the trading spectrum. Order-specific insights from the model can help illuminate expected trading costs and outcomes, and a higher-level view of aggregate predictions can be used to track sentiment, net flows, and intraday changes on an issuer, sector, or market-wide basis. By integrating Tradability into workflows, market participants can better navigate liquidity events and volatility while executing existing orders with greater pre-trade assurance. 

*Tradability scores were capped at 10 during this period. Tradability was later uncapped starting on 5/10/2025, revealing a wider range of scores and more precise predictions.

title: Europe’s bond transparency regimes put data in the spotlight
text:
Europe’s bond transparency regimes put data in the spotlight
It’s no secret that the launch of the US Trade Reporting and Compliance Engine (TRACE) over twenty years ago was a great leap forward for bond markets. Now, UK and European markets are catching up, with regulators set to roll out their latest takes on post-trade transparency. For financial institutions, this is an opportunity to assess the emerging transparency landscape and ensure their data strategies are optimised as the trading environment evolves.
The centrepiece of UK (FCA) and EU (ESMA) transparency efforts is a complete overhaul of the rules governing when transactional data, currently being collected by Approved Publication Arrangements (APAs), can be made available publicly1. This promises a clearer view of market dynamics—an estimated 80-90 percent of corporate bond trades are expected to be published in real time—but also presents challenges for interpretation. While the two frameworks are similar, the differences mean that the price and volume information for the same bond trade could be transmitted to the market at different times, dependent on the reporting entity (Figure 1). While ESMA is broadly more transparent—with maximum deferral times of four weeks compared to the FCA’s three months—there is still no shortage of complexity. A total of 68 different deferral scenarios have been devised for corporate and sovereign bonds across both regimes2.

Figure 1: A comparison of deferral times for corporate bonds under the new transparency regimes. The trade size boundaries are defined to help with comparison.
1An APA is a regulated entity that publishes trade reports on behalf of an investment firm.
2See Table 8 of FCA Policy Statement PS24/14 and tables on pages 45, 46, 49, 50, and 52 in MiFIR review Final Report ESMA74-2134169708-7775.
The introduction of Consolidated Tape Providers (CTPs) for each regulatory regime will go some way to mitigating this complexity, by reducing the number of data sources. This will change from 18 different APAs and dozens of other reporting mechanism to two consolidated feeds. However, market participants will still need not only to assess how best to consume the new datasets available (as well as understand the complexities of the reported data they provide) but also how valuable they are to their organization.
As the leading provider of data to EU and global fixed income markets over the last decade, we’re used to advising clients on how best to determine that value. We know that 3 key factors affect decisions on data consumption and use—quality, coverage and timeliness. In the paragraphs that follow, we take a look at these criteria, examining them in the context of TraX®, our unique source of executed global fixed income data.

Taking the lead on data quality
A comprehensive focus on market transparency means market participants will be required to pay much closer attention to data quality; we know this as a consequence of our continued development of TraX. The breadth and historical scale of the data set—containing 85% of the European and sizeable proportions of the APAC, CEEMEA and other fixed income markets—has provided us with extensive opportunities to continually refine and test its data-cleansing algorithms. Similarly, our users’ pursuit of ever-higher levels of real-time transparency, combined with the robust community of buy- and sell-side clients consuming the data, has helped provide the feedback needed to optimise the testing—and hence the quality.
As a simple comparison, we recently applied these techniques to a population of fixed income trades published by the top 10 APAs and found that almost 40 percent were not usable as-is, requiring extra processing (Figure 2).
Percentage of Clean Trades in the Top 10 APA's
Figure 2: Output from TraX proprietary data-cleansing algorithms on trade data published by the top 10 APAs, covering all fixed income market activity in Q1 2025.
As UK and European trading desks formulate their data strategies, they will need to consider how to balance the potential of regulatory offerings against the work needed to ensure data quality and integrity. With upstream challenges likely to persist, institutions should consider solutions that offer a track record of producing clean, actionable data tailored to market needs.
Getting the most out of coverage
In today’s globalised markets, the deeper and broader the datasets, the more valuable they are. Multiple interconnected markets and trading strategies require a holistic, global view of transaction data. That plays to our strengths as a global trading platform: Our enriched TRACE offering covers the US market, and when combined with the TraX product suite, that completes the global picture. The combined dataset is inclusive of contributions received around the clock, across markets in Europe, APAC, the Americas and beyond (Figure 3).
Corporates by issuer region Q1 2025 v 2024

Sovereigns by issuer region Q1 2025 v 2024
Figure 3: Total volumes collected by the TraX data set in Q1 2025 compared with 2024 across corporate and sovereign bonds.
TraX data is available through a number of live and end-of-day data products. Axess All Prints, our real-time transacted price service and most akin to a TRACE-like offering, publishes daily price prints on over 50,000 executed trades across over 13,000 unique instruments. It has expanded its coverage more than three-fold since launching in 2022, and the team has remained focused on continuously improving the offering. The most recent update to Axess All Prints added clean, real-time pricing for sterling corporates and EM local markets as well as trade direction on every print, increasing average daily trade count coverage by ~15%.
We believe the overlay of the new transparency rules will super-charge the relevancy of our products, allowing for a level of detail on the underlying transactions not previously achievable, all within the regulatory framework. And, with TraX’s contributor-led model, the ability to evolve the product-set in concert with the markets will only further help users to cut through the noise and get precise insights on both primary and secondary markets.
Case Study 1: TraX data to see the full picture
Consider two illustrations:

- In March 2025, as German Bunds moved sharply following news on the country’s fiscal policy, secondary trading volumes spiked as market prices fell. At the time, clients using our TraX Volume data were able to filter out primary market volumes to focus on secondary market trends, as well as understand the client-buy skew in long-term securities.

- In the UK, a continuing news story about the fate of Thames Water linked to controversies over its environmental record and financial viability dominated headlines. TraX users were able to view historical and real-time bond market reactions to these events, not just the total trading volume but also the direction of those flows.

Global, clean, and timely data offers clients a competitive advantage in complex and volatile markets, underscoring the need for a complete data set.
The importance of timeliness
Just as important as what data is available is when it is available. In the both the EU and the UK, regulators have imposed deferral periods for many bond trades. Indeed, some larger trades on less liquid bonds will have to wait to be reported to the market for as long as three months3. TraX, by contrast, receives data directly from (primarily) the dealer community, allowing for a real-time decision on not just when, but how the information should be transmitted4.

3Maximum deferral time under the FCA regime is 3 months, whereas under ESMA it is 4 weeks. Broadly speaking EU reported transactions will be available before the equivalent FCA reported transactions. Deferrals are the responsibility of the transaction reporter.
4TraX receives over 95% of trades in real-time or close to it.
One widely used TraX product is Axess All®, our intra-day trade tape, that provides aggregated & anonymised volume and pricing information for the most actively traded bonds on a 15-minute delay. This innovative approach to transparency means that users can get a more complete view of the actual market dynamics—without the potentially market-moving consequences of publishing the full economics of the most impactful trades.
Once again, our approach allows for the continual refinement and adapts to the evolving needs of market participants. In a world in which information is at a premium, speedier publication can offer market participants a clear advantage.
In summary
As electronic trading continues to expand globally and the regulatory backdrop evolves, the relative performance of different data solutions will feature high on decision makers’ agendas. Their task in the coming months will be to identify products that do the best job of enhancing their trading strategies. In that context, key considerations will include levels of data quality, coverage and timeliness, as well as the presence of value-adds such as extra data fields and customised market intelligence.
We believe TraX and its various derived products offer the best of all worlds—quality, coverage and timeliness in easily-to-consume and ready-packaged solutions designed to meet multiple and various use cases for the data, from front to back office.

From fringe to familiar: The automation frontier in trading
What is the current landscape in the use of automation and algorithms for credit trading?
Since the launch of our first automation tool, Auto-X RFQ in 2018, we've witnessed not only a sharp increase in its adoption but also a transformation in how clients and traders are leveraging it.
We can see that on the client side, utilization rates have surged dramatically. Today, our most advanced automation clients show a 92% Auto-X RFQ utilization rate in US High Grade and 74% in US High Yield - a remarkable leap from 32% and 9% in 2018.
Auto-X RFQ utilization rate surges: A closer look at client automation growth
Smaller lot sizes led the early wave of automation, but the momentum has now decisively moved into larger block sizes. In US High Grade, power users placing orders under 500m are now almost fully automated, while trades above 2mm - once thought too complex (too risky) - now see 39% execution. A similar trend is unfolding in US High Yield: lots of 250m and below are automated at a striking 69%, and even trades over 500m have advanced to 54%.
These trends underscore how automation is no longer limited to smaller trades - it's becoming a trusted tool for handling increasingly larger transactions alongside deeper control and governance options that we discuss below.

Why has Auto-X RFQ quickly become an essential tool for clients?
Client trading objectives are clear: maximize efficiency, reduce execution costs, and unlock opportunities for price improvement. Auto-X RFQ delivers on all three fronts. It is a powerful, intelligent, yet simple to use rules-based tool that enables clients to achieve these goals by automating all or part of the trading execution workflow.
The advantages Auto-X RFQ are twofold. First, is the unparalleled sophistication it delivers for data-driven decision-making. It is powered by CP+™, an Al-powered pricing engine for global credit and rate markets. By combining the extensive data from the MarketAxess trading platform with public TRACE and proprietary TraX inputs, CP+ equips clients with unmatched accuracy in price discovery, transaction cost analysis, and algorithmic strategies. Complementing this is the relative liquidity score, which provides a precise measure of a bond's tradability and market depth.
Second, is its dynamic waterfall approach to rule setting. Automation criteria can be set and refined using simple variables such as trade size, price, number of respondents and more. With our parameter modeling tool, clients can use their historical data to assess and predict the likely impact of automation and its effect on overall performance. This flexibility enables higher automation rates, greater efficiency in larger trades—including blocks—and the ability to deploy multiple custom rule sets across markets.

What does this look like from the dealer perspective?
Dealer pricing algorithms are gaining ground in block trades, with the strongest growth seen in the 2mm-5mm bucket range. Not only are dealer algos responding more, but they're also winning more - moving from a 10% win rate in 2023 to 25% in 2025 for credit block inquiries.

title: How trades move markets: a data driven exploration of market impact
text:
How trades move markets: a data driven exploration of market impact
Executive Summary

- Market impact is measurable and manageable. It is driven by liquidity, size, and execution choice.

- Median post-trade impact is 13% of the bid-ask spread in US HG and 11% in EUR IG.

- Liquidity matters most: low-liquidity US HG bonds show nearly twice the median impact of high-liquidity bonds.

- Size matters but not indefinitely: impact rises up to about $2 million, then largely plateaus. 

- When market interest aligns with the trade, post-trade price impact tends to be amplified; when it runs counter, the impact is often muted.

- All-to-all trading such as Open Trading®, does not incur the information leakage cost many assume; broader liquidity access does not appear to drive a proportionate increase in market impact. 

Introduction
Market impact is commonly seen as the unavoidable cost of revealing trading intent. Every trade signals information to the market, and that signal helps form the next price. The assumption is that the more broadly a trade is distributed, the more the market learns, the more prices are expected to move. It suggests a trade-off between access to liquidity, price competition, and information leakage. This shapes how traders think about counterparty selection, potentially confining how widely they send inquiries and how much competition they invite.
But analyzing the data more comprehensively tells a different story. It shows that market impact is not primarily determined by information leakage associated with broader distribution. It is driven first by liquidity, then by trade size, and finally by execution choice, with prevailing market conditions such as market skew further influencing outcomes. Additionally, the penalty for broader distribution is often smaller than traditionally expected. In many cases, expanding access to liquidity, including through Open Trading, does not meaningfully increase post-trade price movement. Counterparty selection, then, need not be constrained. It can be used as an important tool to balance competition and the dissemination of trading interest. 
Methodology
To measure impact, we need a benchmark that updates frequently and reflects where the market is trading in real time. We use CP+™, our AI-driven pricing model, because it provides 99% coverage across the relevant universe and refreshes every 15 seconds on average. Our measure looks at the move in CP+ mid spread in the minutes after each trade, 30 minutes unless otherwise noted. We isolate the price component of spread changes so the result reflects the effect of the trade itself rather than broader benchmark moves. We then sign the move so a positive value represents movement in the direction of the trade, tightening for buys and widening for sells. 

 I =

 (Spread+n − Spread0) * −DV010

 Bid_Ask_Spread0

 * Sign

The sample includes 186,000 US High Grade trades and 52,000 EUR Investment Grade trades executed on MarketAxess in H2 2025. It covers notional sizes from $150,000 to $25 million and only includes trades executed within one bid-ask spread of CP+ (see Appendix for additional details).

Measuring impact
Trades do move markets. In the 30 minutes before a trade, prices can move by as much as 33% of bid-ask spread, but the median move is 0%. After the trade, the distribution shifts meaningfully: post-trade moves reach 76% in US HG and 62% in EUR IG, with median moves of 13% and 11%, respectively. The takeaway: post-trade repricing is real, measurable, and distinct from normal market noise.

The bands represent the middle 45th to 55th, 35th to 65th, 25th to 75th, 15th to 85th and 5th to 95th percentile of trade impact outcomes. Collectively, they represent the distribution of post-trade price movements by timestamp.

EUR IG median impact relative to trade time

How to Read: Rows show trade outcome percentiles; columns indicate time relative to execution. For example, 5% at +30m means 5% of trades move more than 34% against the trade in 30 minutes, while 95% shows 5% move more than 76% in favor.

Liquidity
Liquidity is the strongest predictor of market impact. When the bond is harder to trade, the market moves more to absorb the transaction. In US HG, bonds with a low Relative Liquidity Score of 1-3 show a median impact of 19% of bid-ask spread, versus 11% for bonds with a high score of 8-10. In EUR IG, the gap is smaller but still visible at 12% versus 10%. The same pattern appears even more clearly in Tradability, our AI-driven response count prediction solution: bonds expected to receive fewer than five responses show a median impact of 18% in US HG and 12% in EUR IG, while bonds likely to receive more than ten prices back show 10% and 9%, respectively.
The difference is more pronounced in US HG because the liquidity spread between the easiest and hardest bonds to trade is wider. In US HG, bonds with a liquidity score of 1 have a median CP+ bid-ask spread that's 10.9x wider than those with a score of 10. In EUR IG, that gap is 3.7x.
How to Read: The charts below illustrate the median impact (as a percentage of bid ask spread) by liquidity profile across different time deltas.

US HG median impact relative to trade time by RLS bucket
EUR IG median impact relative to trade time by RLS bucket

US HG median impact relative to trade time by tradability bucket

EUR IG median impact relative to trade time by tradability bucket

Trade size
Trade size plays a significant role in market impact, with larger deals typically causing greater disruption. However, this effect diminishes in transactions above $2 million in notional size. Trades with less than $500,000 in notional volume typically have a median impact of 13% of the bid-ask spread (10% in EUR IG). For trades between $1 million and $2 million, the median impact increases to 16% (13% in EUR IG). Transactions exceeding $2 million see an impact of 19% in US HG (13% in EUR IG), which remains consistent for larger trade sizes. This plateau can be partially attributed to what information about trades are revealed to the entire market.
US HG trades are reported to TRACE, meaning the market (CP+ included), receives trade information from this source. US HG trades are capped at $5 million notional in TRACE. This results in all trades over $5 million having the same informational footprint from the TRACE tape, except to the parties invited to the inquiry. However, the minimal difference in impact between $2 million and $5 million trades, where the true size of the trade is disclosed, indicates that increasing volumes beyond $2 million do not substantially increase market disruption. In EUR IG, trade tapes are not as common, resulting in less transparency around trade volume. This is likely to contribute to the reduced variation in market impact across volume in EUR IG. In summary, while larger trade sizes do tend to have more influence, their effect may be less significant than anticipated. 
US HG median impact relative to trade volume by volume bucket
EUR IG median impact relative to trade volume by volume bucket

Market skew
Execution quality depends not just on bond liquidity, but on which side of the market already shows interest. Market impact increases when one side shows strong interest, as measured by our Tradability skew, the gap between bid and offer predictions. When a trade aligns with the prevailing skew, indicating strong interest from one side, the average effect rises to around 17% of the bid-ask spread in US HG and 13% in EUR IG. In the absence of skew, the average impact drops to 13% in US HG and 11% in EUR IG. Conversely, trades executed against the skew experience a reduced average impact of 8% in both US HG and EUR IG. When the market is already leaning one way, trading into that imbalance is materially more expensive than trading against it. 
US HG median impact by tradability skew and trade side
EUR IG median impact by tradability skew and trade side

Counterparty selection
Broader distribution does not appear to carry the market impact penalty many investors assume. Counterparty selection is a real execution lever because it shapes the trade-off between price competition and information leakage. But the trade-off is not binary. The data suggests traders can often widen access to liquidity without paying a proportionate cost in post-trade repricing.
On average, adding three counterparties is associated with roughly 1% of bid-ask spread in extra price improvement, which means broader distribution can create real competitive value. Just as important, the impact cost remains contained. In US HG, including the Open Trading liquidity pool on an inquiry already being sent to a list of disclosed dealers produces roughly the same median post-trade price movement as sending it to just a disclosed dealer list. In EUR IG, the pattern is similar: median post-trade movement is about 10% of bid-ask spread when sent to fewer than 10 disclosed dealers, and about 13% when sent to more than 10 dealers — the same 13% observed when Open Trading is included. The takeaway: access to all-to-all liquidity is not the market impact penalty box. For many trades, it can expand competition without meaningfully changing the repricing outcome. 
US HG median impact relative to trade time by OT/DD status & invited dealers
EUR IG median impact relative to trade time by OT/DD status & invited dealers

Conclusion
Market impact is real, but it is hierarchical. Using CP+ as a high-frequency benchmark, this analysis demonstrates a consistent post-trade drift in the direction of the liquidity taker. It is driven first by liquidity, then by size, and then by execution choice, with the information leakage cost of all-to-all trading smaller than commonly assumed. 
That matters because liquidity and size are observable before a trade happens. Traders can use liquidity signals such as our Relative Liquidity Score and Tradability to better judge where impact is likely to be highest, how broadly to distribute an inquiry, and when stronger competition is worth the risk of signaling intent. 
Execution strategy should adapt to the expected impact profile of the trade. Smaller and more liquid trades can often support broader competition. Larger and less liquid trades may still call for more selective distribution. 
The takeaway is clear: worries around information leakage should not deter traders from accessing all-to-all price competitiveness. Ultimately, market impact is primarily driven by liquidity, trade size, and market conditions with the size of the liquidity pool being less of a concern. 

Research note
Using CP+ as a benchmark does have an important limitation. The model incorporates the traded level into its next prediction, so wide trades tend to pull the estimate wider and tight trades tend to pull it tighter. CP+ Under the Hood explains this in more detail. In practice, trades still tend to push pricing in the direction of the transaction, even when they print tighter than CP+, validating our findings. Wide trades show a stronger effect because the model signal and the market signal reinforce each other, while tight trades create a conflicting signal. To isolate the market-driven effect rather than CP+ model adjustments, we filtered our sample only on trades where CP+ was within one bid-ask spread of the traded level. That helps ensure the moves we observe are driven more by market activity than by the model adjusting to atypical prints.
US HG impact by trade delta
EUR IG impact by trade delta
The dataset, like CP+ as a whole, shows no bias towards wide or tight predictions, with both outcomes occurring equally often. This validates our methodology, as the CP+ features that adapt to traded levels respond similarly to widening and tightening across samples. We conducted this analysis on both US HG and EUR IG CP+ models, demonstrating that our results are consistent across markets and models.

title: Opportunities for global investors as China further opens its cross-border bond market
text:
Opportunities for global investors as China further opens its cross-border bond market
I recently had the privilege of attending the Bond Connect Anniversary Summit 2025 in Hong Kong on behalf of MarketAxess. With the theme “Unlocking Value through China’s Resilience”, the summit brought together regulators, investors, and market participants from Mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and other regions. 
In this article, I would like to share my key takeaways on the latest trends and strategic insights on China’s bond market, and the growing role of RMB-denominated assets in global investment portfolios. 
Further opening of China’s financial markets 
As the world's second-largest bond market, China's financial landscape offers a diverse set of instruments and sophisticated mechanisms, drawing strong interest from overseas investors. 
At the Summit, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) jointly announced a number of major initiatives aimed at further opening China’s financial markets and deepening cross-border connectivity. These include expanding the investor base for Southbound Bond Connect, enhancing offshore repo arrangements, updating collateral and margin requirements, and improving the Swap Connect mechanism. These measures are widely seen as critical steps to strengthen Hong Kong’s role as a global financial hub and to promote the internationalization of the RMB.
The appeal of RMB bonds and their value in global portfolios
RMB bonds are increasingly viewed as a stable and appealing option for global investors, offering diversification benefits alongside competitive total returns and Sharpe ratios. Their low correlation with major global markets, combined with improving market liquidity, has made them increasingly popular among international investors.
The inclusion of RMB bonds in major global indices—such as the Bloomberg Global Aggregate, WGBI, and GBI-EM—has further boosted foreign interest. As new repo arrangements are rolled out and liquidity improves, many investors believe there is more room to optimize performance through effective trading strategies and collateral management. Nevertheless, investors remain mindful of how macroeconomic uncertainties such as global market volatility, geopolitical tensions, and shifts in monetary policy might impact capital flows and investor sentiment.
Hong Kong's unique role in facilitating the RMB ecosystem
Hong Kong continues to serve as a key offshore hub for the RMB market, offering a strong financial infrastructure and a solid regulatory framework. During the summit, several proposals were presented to strengthen Hong Kong's position: 

- Boosting primary market issuance of RMB bonds, particularly Dim Sum bonds and Panda bonds, to further internationalize the RMB and establish an offshore RMB yield curve.

- Expanding RMB derivative markets to facilitate capital flows in response to interest rate and exchange rate volatility, thereby creating a more effective price discovery mechanism.

- Launching RMB-denominated gold trading in Hong Kong and developing an RMB-based pricing mechanism.

- Optimizing Bond Connect by broadening access to corporate bonds and extending bond durations, which has already driven higher volumes. There were also proposals to expand the range of collateral to improve market efficiency and reduce transaction costs.

Opportunities and challenges for electronic trading platforms
The continued evolution of Bond Connect places e-trading platforms at the center of China’s bond market transformation. These platforms now play a pivotal role in serving a broader base of global investors, offering tools that support cross-border, multi-currency trading, and incorporating features that align with international best practices.
As a key e-trading partner of Bond Connect, MarketAxess has seen significant growth in both trading volume and client activity on the Northbound channel. As China’s cross-border bond market landscape continues to evolve, ongoing innovation will be crucial to meet the increasingly complex needs of both regional and global market participants. 
Recent data shows a steady increase in net foreign inflows into Chinese Government Bonds (CGBs). However, foreign ownership of Local Market (LM) bonds remains relatively low compared to other Asian and global economies, underscoring the untapped potential in China’s expanding cross-border bond market.

title: ICE Launches MSCI® MarketAxess Tradable Corporate Bond Index Futures to Help Investors Hedge Corporate Bond Exposure
text:
NEW YORK & LONDON--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- 
 Intercontinental Exchange, Inc. (NYSE: ICE), a leading global provider of technology and data, and home to the most liquid markets for trading MSCI®
 futures, today announced the launch of MSCI® MarketAxess Tradable Corporate Bond Index futures.

The futures contracts will be based on MSCI and MarketAxess’ newly created corporate bond indices. These tradable indices aim to provide a benchmark for the performance of the corporate bond market, incorporating sector and credit allocation to ensure low tracking error to the MSCI parent indices and reliable replication of the credit market.

“The introduction of ICE MSCI MarketAxess Corporate Bond futures are a welcome addition to the existing suite of credit futures,” said Antony Harden, Executive Director, Goldman Sachs. “Timing couldn’t be better as client adoption hits an all-time high as credit futures find their way into investors toolkits.”

ICE’s four futures contracts offer a way for institutional investors to integrate corporate bond hedges into their investment process and are based on the following indices: MSCI MarketAxess USD IG Tradable Corporate Bond Index, MSCI MarketAxess USD HY Tradable Corporate Bond Index, MSCI MarketAxess EUR IG Tradable Corporate Bond Index and MSCI MarketAxess EUR HY Tradable Corporate Bond Index.

The MSCI MarketAxess Tradable Corporate bond indices methodology uses MarketAxess’ Relative Liquidity Scores to identify and measure the performance of a selection of liquid fixed income securities from MSCI’s broader Corporate Bond Indices.

“ICE’s markets account for over 70% of global MSCI futures trading by volume in equity markets, and we are pleased to expand our relationship to the corporate bond futures market,” said Caterina Caramaschi, Vice President, Financial Derivatives, ICE. “The launch reflects growing investor demand for products that allow better management of corporate bond portfolios, and we thank MSCI and MarketAxess for their collaboration.”

"We are excited to be working with ICE and MarketAxess to provide investors with innovative tools designed to manage credit exposures more efficiently,” said George Harrington, Managing Director, MSCI. “By leveraging MSCI's index methodologies, MarketAxess' unique liquidity metrics and ICE's leading trading platform, clients can efficiently trade and achieve enhanced liquidity.”

“Credit futures are an important tool for a healthy market and our institutional clients—one that will generate more liquidity in the cash markets,” said Kat Sweeney, Global Head of Data and ETF Solutions at MarketAxess. “We are proud to have introduced these tradable indices with MSCI and are equally excited to be expanding on our data and trading relationship with ICE with the launch of these futures.”

ICE’s MSCI MarketAxess Tradable Corporate Bond Index Futures will join ICE’s existing suite of liquid futures based on MSCI ACWI, MSCI EAFE, MSCI Emerging Markets, MSCI ESG and MSCI Climate indices, providing participants around the world with a set of tools to manage equity risk. So far in 2024, the average daily volume for ICE’s MSCI complex is over 190,000 contracts, equal to an estimated $13.6 billion of notional value. Approximately 45 million ICE MSCI futures contracts have traded year-to-date.

title: MarketAxess Expands AI-Powered Pricing Engine to Cover Municipal Bonds

CP+™ real-time pricing now available on the fastest growing electronic muni marketplace 

NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- MarketAxess Holdings Inc. (Nasdaq: MKTX), the operator of a leading electronic trading platform for fixed-income securities, today announced that CP+, the AI-powered, algorithmic pricing engine for global credit and rates markets, will now also cover municipal bonds.
By leveraging proprietary data from the MarketAxess trading platform, TraX® market data, and public sources like TRACE, CP+ goes beyond traditional fixed income pricing sources to deliver value across the entire investment lifecycle—from portfolio construction and price discovery to end-of-day pricing validation. With this expansion of coverage, MarketAxess clients trading munis will benefit from accurate and unbiased reference pricing for the MSRB-reportable municipal bond universe.
“We are excited to see the difference the introduction of real-time, AI-powered algorithmic pricing can make to a historically fragmented market like municipal bonds. Our award-winning models excel at extracting pricing signals from multiple data sources, which is crucial in munis where trading is known to be sporadic,” says Julien Alexandre, Global Head of Research at MarketAxess.
“The muni marketplace has seen notable e-trading growth in recent years, and we believe innovations like CP+ with real-time, actionable data for ~930,000 municipal bonds will not only increase transparency and efficiency, but also the speed of adoption for electronic trading,” says Daniel Kelly, Head of Municipal Securities at MarketAxess.
First introduced to the market in 2017, CP+ is a critical data input and pricing source for multiple MarketAxess trading protocols and solutions, including Auto-X ™ and Portfolio Trading. For more information on MarketAxess muni solutions and CP+, visit: https://www.marketaxess.com/trade/municipal-bonds
About MarketAxess
MarketAxess (Nasdaq: MKTX) operates a leading electronic trading platform that delivers greater trading efficiency, a diversified pool of liquidity and significant cost savings to institutional investors and broker-dealers across the global fixed-income markets. Over 2,000 firms leverage MarketAxess’ patented technology to efficiently trade fixed-income securities. title: AxessPoint: Intraday liquidity trends
text:
AxessPoint: Intraday liquidity trends
This AxessPoint takes a look at intraday liquidity trends and the factors that impact this activity. A deep dive reveals that access to liquidity is strong throughout the trading day as indicated by cost of trading and depth of liquidity. We start by looking at market liquidity through the traded volumes in US IG and EU IG that are reported to TRACE and TraX®, respectively. 
Highlights
Intraday trends in volume are driven by liquidity taker workflow, not liquidity provider activity.
Access to liquidity is strong throughout the trading day as indicated by cost of trading and depth of liquidity.
Liquidity Taker Activity
We first look at market liquidity through the traded volumes in US IG and EU IG that are reported to TRACE and TraX®, respectively.
In US IG, 10% of trading volume is reported at the precise moment of benchmark price determination—a process known as "spotting," where trades are logged at the exact time the benchmark's price is established. 11am, 3pm and 4pm are the most common spot times. 12% of client submitted RFQs on MarketAxess by trade volume use a delayed spot. For this analysis, we remove TRACE prints that occurred at common spot times as the spread for these trades could have been agreed upon at any point prior in the day.
Both US IG and EU IG volumes exhibit dips and peaks throughout the day. At first glance, this might suggest a changing liquidity landscape. However, understanding the full market dynamic requires a deeper dive into the driving forces behind executed volumes.
Distribution of Traded Volume
Figure 1 | Bins represent 15-min sum. Time is local (London for TraX, New York for TRACE)
We further analyze the client-initiated inquiries on the MarketAxess platform. Our findings reveal that requested volume trends closely mirror those of executed volumes, indicating that executed volume patterns are influenced by the actions of liquidity takers.
Distribution of Inquiry Volume on MarketAxess
Figure 2 | Time is local (London for EU IG, New York for US IG)
Through inquiry volumes and executed volumes, we observe trading patterns of liquidity takers. We now examine cost of trading and depth of liquidity intraday, which gives alternative measures of liquidity.
Cost of Trading
By using CP+™, which is the MarketAxess AI powered algorithmic bond pricing engine, and more particularly CP+ Bid-Ask Spread, we can evaluate pre-trade cost of trading. The B/A spread gives the expected round trip cost. In both US IG and EU IG, trading costs decline in the first hour of the day before remaining close to constant for the rest of the session.
CP+ Bid-Ask Spread
Figure 3 | Difference between CP+ bid and ask predictions. Time is local.
We can also look at the realized cost of trading on the MarketAxess Platform. For this, we use Transaction Cost Analysis (TCA) which is the delta between executed level and CP+ of the corresponding side. Investors obtained constant TCA throughout the day. TCA in H1 2024 was 1 cent in US IG and 0 in EU IG on client initiated.
TCA on MarketAxess
Figure 4 | Cost of transaction compared to CP+. Time is local.
Depth of Liquidity
Strong access to liquidity is further seen through Tradability, MarketAxess’ AI-powered gauge of liquidity that predicts the expected number of disclosed and anonymous responses a given inquiry will receive on the MarketAxess platform.
A higher Tradability signals a deeper market. In both US IG and EU IG, Tradability climbs for the first hour of the day, before remaining constant for the rest of the session. This consistency further supports our finding that access to liquidity remains stable from 9:00am till market close.
Tradability Predictions
Figure 5 | Average Tradability. Time is local.
While Tradability measures the expected depth of the market, the realized number of responses to an RFQ gauges actual depth of market. In both US IG and EU IG, the average number of responses from a liquidity provider remains strong from 9:00am onward – with 12.31 responses per inquiry in US IG and 10.60 responses per inquiry in EU IG in H1 2024. The stability of responsiveness strengthens our conclusion of sustained access to liquidity from 9:00am till market close.
Responses Per Inquiry on MarketAxess
Figure 6 | Average responses throughout trading day. Time is local.
Conclusion
Both predicted and realized trading costs and depth of liquidity provision exhibit that liquidity is strong and constant intraday. Liquidity providers supply consistent liquidity all day. Patterns in overall volumes can be explained by liquidity taker workflow. Traders should feel comfortable accessing liquidity all day long.
CP+ is MarketAxess’ proprietary AI powered pricing engine for corporate bonds. It produces an unbiased, two-sided market for more than 33,000 instruments globally. Updated every 15 to 60 seconds, the engine generates nearly 30 million levels per day covering 90-95% of trading activity in its markets.
Tradability is MarketAxess’ proprietary AI powered liquidity metric for corporate bonds. It assesses the market’s capacity to provide immediate pricing to a specific order. It predicts the number of responses to a given RFQ inquiry pre-trade and is size and side specific. It covers nearly 18,000 bonds.
TraX data from MarketAxess aggregates bond market activity executed by European banks, asset managers and trading firms across both voice and electronic trading methods that is validated in near real-time through a post-trade regulatory reporting and trade confirmation engine.

title: Rick McVey to Retire from MarketAxess
text:
Carlos Hernandez Elected As Next Chairman

 NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- 
MarketAxess Holdings Inc. (Nasdaq: MKTX), the operator of a leading electronic trading platform for fixed-income securities, today announced that Founder and Executive Chairman Rick McVey will retire at the end of the year. Carlos Hernandez will succeed Mr. McVey as Chairman of the Board of Directors, effective January 1, 2025. Mr. McVey has agreed to remain as the Chairman of the Board of Directors of MarketAxess Limited, the Company’s international holding company.

Mr. McVey founded MarketAxess in 2000 and is a visionary in the evolution of fixed income market structure. Under his leadership, the company grew to become a global, S&P 500 company that has transformed the way the world’s largest capital market operates worldwide. Mr. McVey stepped down as CEO of MarketAxess in April 2023 after 23 years in that role, and has since been serving as Executive Chairman of the Board.

“Rick’s bold vision for the company nearly 25 years ago not only revolutionized trading forever, but also created an outstanding organization in the process,” said Chris Concannon, CEO of MarketAxess. “I’d like to congratulate Rick on an incredible accomplishment and thank him for the opportunity to lead the company as we continue to transform global markets.”

"The last quarter century has been an incredible journey, and it was an honor to lead this organization from a startup to a position of global leadership. None of this could have been possible without the skill and dedication of our management team, employees, and board of directors,” said Mr. McVey. “Most importantly, I am grateful for the tremendous support we enjoy from our dealer and investor clients around the world. The future of MarketAxess is bright and I am confident under Chris' leadership we will continue our track record of innovation and growth to create lasting improvements for global fixed income markets. I look forward to my continued involvement on the Board of MarketAxess Limited as we continue to expand our reach in international financial markets."

Mr. Hernandez previously served as a Director from 2006 to 2019 and rejoined the MarketAxess Board in September 2023. Mr. Hernandez, who is designated as an independent Director, currently serves as the Chair of the Board’s Compensation and Talent Committee. Mr. Hernandez retired from JPMorgan in April 2023 after 37 years of service. Prior to his retirement, Mr. Hernandez was Executive Chair of Investment and Corporate Banking at JPMorgan and served as a Member of the Operating Committee and a Member of the Corporate & Investment Bank Management Team.

“Having watched firsthand this incredible company that Rick McVey built, consistently challenge norms, break records and set new standards for fixed-income electronification for over two decades—I am incredibly honored to succeed him as Chairman,” said Mr. Hernandez. “I look forward to working closely with Chris Concannon and our seasoned management team during this next phase of MarketAxess as we find new ways to make one of the world’s leading fixed income marketplaces even better.”

 About MarketAxess

 MarketAxess (Nasdaq: MKTX) operates a leading electronic trading platform that delivers greater trading efficiency, a diversified pool of liquidity and significant cost savings to institutional investors and broker-dealers across the global fixed-income markets. Over 2,000 firms leverage MarketAxess’ patented technology to efficiently trade fixed-income securities. Our automated and algorithmic trading solutions, combined with our integrated and actionable data offerings, help our clients make faster, better-informed decisions on when and how to trade on our platform. MarketAxess’ award-winning Open Trading® marketplace is widely regarded as the preferred all-to-all trading solution in the global credit markets. Founded in 2000, MarketAxess connects a robust network of market participants through an advanced full trading lifecycle solution that includes automated trading solutions, intelligent data and index products and a range of post-trade services.  For periods beginning with January 2024, the Company has made changes to the market volume data used to calculate estimated market share for Municipal and U.S. Government Bonds. For Municipal Bonds, the Company previously used estimates, derived from data issued by the Municipal Securities Rule Making Board (“MSRB”), including estimates for new issuance, commercial paper and variable-rate trading activity, and excluded these volumes from the estimated market volume data. While the Company still uses estimates, the new methodology for identifying and excluding these volumes from the market volume data is now based on MSRB “flags” to identify new issuance, commercial paper, and variable-rate volumes. For U.S. Government Bonds, the previous data source for estimated market volumes was the Federal Reserve Bank’s Reported Primary Dealer U.S. Treasury Bond Trading Volumes, which was reported on a one-week lag. The new source for U.S. Government Bond trading volumes is FINRA’s U.S. Treasury TRACE data. The Company believes that the refined methodology used for Municipal Bonds, and the new data source for U.S. Government Bonds, provides more accurate measures of estimated market volumes and estimated market share. Prior comparable periods have been recast retrospectively for both Municipal and U.S. Government Bonds to conform to the updated presentation of the data. The new estimated market volume data is also available on the Company’s website at
